term: Universal Forwarder file monitoring — Splunk on-premises
definition: Agent • Universal Forwarder • Splunk-to-Splunk with Splunk on-premises as the final destination.
relationshipRule: Current logging pattern classified under TAX-03.02.01 The final indexed destination is Splunk on-premises.
notes: This destination-specific variant terminates in Splunk on-premises.

fields.Pattern Name: Universal Forwarder file monitoring — Splunk on-premises
fields.Required App / TA: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux or vendor TA
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise indexer or indexer cluster
fields.Forwarding / Delivery: Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS, HEC, local modular input, file monitoring or another supported Splunk Enterprise ingestion path
fields.Destination Processing: Props/transforms on the appropriate parsing tier, index-time routing, masking and sourcetype assignment before indexing
fields.Destination Health Checks: Indexer availability, licensing, queues, forwarding success, input status, indexing latency and event freshness
fields.Destination Governance: Validate local app compatibility, indexer or heavy-forwarder placement, approved indexes, retention and infrastructure ownership
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow TCP 9997 to the receiving indexer cluster or approved Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation paths.
fields.Authentication Requirements: The forwarder service account requires read access to the selected files or Windows channels. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust; no source API key is required.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Define monitored file paths or Windows channels, file ownership and permissions, log rotation behaviour, hostname handling, index, sourcetype and expected event volume. Record the deployment server and receiving target.

term: Universal Forwarder file monitoring — Splunk Cloud
definition: Agent • Universal Forwarder • Splunk-to-Splunk with Splunk Cloud as the final destination.
relationshipRule: Current logging pattern classified under TAX-03.02.01 The final indexed destination is Splunk Cloud.
notes: This destination-specific variant terminates in Splunk Cloud.

fields.Pattern Name: Universal Forwarder file monitoring — Splunk Cloud
fields.Required App / TA: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux or vendor TA
fields.Forwarding / Delivery: Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS, HEC, cloud-supported modular input, or another Splunk Cloud-supported ingestion path
fields.Destination Processing: Optional Ingest Processor or Edge Processor routing, masking, filtering and sourcetype assignment before indexing
fields.Destination Health Checks: Splunk Cloud index availability, ingestion latency, forwarding success, HEC or input status, pipeline status and event freshness
fields.Destination Governance: Validate Splunk Cloud support, app compatibility, approved indexes, data residency and tenant permissions
fields.Technical Requirements: Outbound TCP 9997 from the Universal Forwarder to <instance>.splunkcloud.com for event forwarding; outbound TCP 8089 from the Universal Forwarder to the deployment server for deployment management.
fields.Required Network Flows: Universal Forwarder → <instance>.splunkcloud.com on TCP 9997; Universal Forwarder → deployment server on TCP 8089.
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation paths.
fields.Authentication Requirements: The forwarder service account requires read access to the selected files or Windows channels. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust; no source API key is required.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Define monitored file paths or Windows channels, file ownership and permissions, log rotation behaviour, hostname handling, index, sourcetype and expected event volume. Record the deployment server and receiving target.

fields.Pattern Name: Syslog via SC4S — Splunk on-premises
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise indexer or indexer cluster
fields.Forwarding / Delivery: Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS, HEC, local modular input, file monitoring or another supported Splunk Enterprise ingestion path
fields.Destination Processing: Props/transforms on the appropriate parsing tier, index-time routing, masking and sourcetype assignment before indexing
fields.Destination Health Checks: Indexer availability, licensing, queues, forwarding success, input status, indexing latency and event freshness
fields.Destination Governance: Validate local app compatibility, indexer or heavy-forwarder placement, approved indexes, retention and infrastructure ownership
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow source devices to SC4S on UDP/TCP 514 or TCP 6514 for TLS, as selected; allow TCP 8088 or 443 from SC4S to the approved on-premises HEC endpoint. Restrict listeners to approved source networks.
fields.Authentication Requirements: UDP/TCP syslog normally has no application credential. For TLS syslog, configure server certificates and optionally mutual TLS. SC4S requires a dedicated Splunk HEC token for onward delivery.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Record each device or platform hostname/IP, vendor and product, destination SC4S address, protocol and port, facility/severity, message template, timezone and expected EPS. Configure the matching SC4S vendor source and metadata rules.

term: Splunk Stream network traffic collection — Splunk Cloud
definition: Splunk Stream pattern for capturing network traffic or wire data, extracting protocol metadata, and sending structured events to Splunk with Splunk Cloud as the final destination.
relationshipRule: A Stream Forwarder or supported packet-capture component observes network traffic, applies Splunk Stream protocol configuration, and forwards structured flow or protocol events to Splunk Cloud or Splunk indexers The final indexed destination is Splunk Cloud.
notes: Use this as a dedicated logging pattern rather than treating Splunk Stream only as an app or add-on. The Splunk Stream app/add-on supports the pattern, while the pattern defines the end-to-end collection architecture. This destination-specific variant terminates in Splunk Cloud.

fields.Required App / TA: Splunk App for Stream and associated Stream components

fields.Security Considerations: Limit capture scope, protect sensitive payloads, prefer metadata-only collection where appropriate, and apply filtering or masking requirements
fields.Failure Behaviour: Alert on capture loss, packet drops, stale forwarders, blocked forwarding, unexpected volume changes and missing protocol events
fields.Forwarding / Delivery: Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS, HEC, cloud-supported modular input, or another Splunk Cloud-supported ingestion path

definition: Source cannot send directly to Splunk on-premises and must first send to a Splunk Heavy Forwarder. This may be required because of firewall policy, security-zone boundaries, network segmentation, protocol restrictions, local processing requirements or unsupported direct connectivity.
relationshipRule: Source M:1 Heavy Forwarder; Heavy Forwarder M:1 Splunk Enterprise destination. The Heavy Forwarder is the required intermediary collection and forwarding tier.
notes: Use where direct connectivity is unavailable or prohibited, including firewall restrictions, DMZ or security-zone separation, network segmentation, restricted routing, one-way egress policy, local protocol termination, local app/add-on execution, or local parsing and routing requirements.

fields.Pattern Name: Heavy Forwarder intermediary — Splunk on-premises
fields.Source Mechanism: Syslog, API, database, file, HEC or other supported input
fields.Source-to-HF Transport: Vendor-supported protocol such as syslog, HTTPS, JDBC, file monitoring or HEC
fields.Processing / Routing: Local app/add-on input, protocol termination, checkpointing, parsing, props/transforms, filtering, masking, enrichment and index routing
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise indexer or indexer cluster
fields.Required App / TA: Install on the Heavy Forwarder when the app/add-on should not run on the indexer tier
fields.Default Health Profile: Source connectivity, input status, app/add-on health, authentication, checkpoint age, event lag, parsing, persistent queue, tcpout queue, forwarding status and indexer freshness
fields.Failure Behaviour: Queue and retry where supported; alert on firewall denies, connection timeouts, TLS failures, blocked routes, sustained queue growth, stale checkpoints and end-to-end delivery failure
fields.Pattern Selection Reasons: Firewall restrictions; security-zone or DMZ boundaries; network segmentation; restricted routing; source cannot reach the final Splunk destination; only approved intermediary hosts may cross zones; local protocol termination; local app/add-on requirement; parsing, masking or enrichment requirement
fields.Firewall / Security Zone Use Case: Place the Heavy Forwarder in an approved intermediary zone with permitted inbound connectivity from the source zone and permitted outbound connectivity to the Splunk destination. Avoid opening direct source-to-destination paths when policy requires controlled zone traversal.
fields.Required Network Flows: Source zone → Heavy Forwarder on the source protocol; Heavy Forwarder → final Splunk destination using approved TLS forwarding or HEC. Document source, destination, port, protocol, direction, security zone and firewall rule owner.
fields.Security Controls: Least-privilege firewall rules, TLS, certificate validation, restricted service accounts, persistent queues, hardened Heavy Forwarder, administrative access controls, logging of blocked connections and regular firewall-rule review
fields.Network Health Checks: Source-to-HF reachability, listener availability, firewall deny events, TLS handshake success, HF-to-destination reachability, connection resets, retransmissions, queue growth and end-to-end freshness
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow only the source-specific protocol from the source security zone to the approved Heavy Forwarder; allow TCP 9997 to the receiving indexer cluster or approved Heavy Forwarder from the Heavy Forwarder to the final destination; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. fields.Authentication Requirements: Use the source-supported credential on the Heavy Forwarder, such as OAuth, API key, service account, certificate, database account or HEC token. Use dedicated Splunk TLS certificates for onward forwarding and keep source secrets in the approved credential store.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Provide the source endpoint and protocol, source and destination security zones, required app/add-on, input stanza, tenant/account IDs where applicable, parsing and routing rules, expected volume, target index/sourcetype, destination group and failover behaviour.

term: No add-on: HEC collector via Heavy Forwarder — Splunk on-premises
definition: No Splunk app or add-on is available. The source sends events to HEC on an intermediary Heavy Forwarder, which validates, processes and forwards them to Splunk Enterprise.
relationshipRule: Source M:1 HEC collector on Heavy Forwarder; HEC collector M:1 Splunk Enterprise destination. The Heavy Forwarder is mandatory and provides the controlled collection boundary.
notes: Use when the source has native HEC or HTTPS push capability but no supported Splunk app or add-on exists, and direct access to the on-premises indexer tier is unavailable or prohibited.

fields.Pattern Category: Custom HEC integration without vendor app/add-on
fields.Source Mechanism: Source-native HTTPS push to Splunk HEC
fields.Add-on / App Availability: No supported Splunk app or add-on is available
fields.Intermediary Platform: Splunk Heavy Forwarder acting as HEC collector
fields.HEC Configuration: Dedicated HEC token, approved source and sourcetype, target index, TLS certificate, channel where indexer acknowledgement is used, and least-privilege token permissions
fields.Processing / Routing: HEC token routing, metadata assignment, validation, optional line breaking, timestamp extraction, props/transforms, filtering, masking, enrichment and onward forwarding
fields.Required App / TA: None; use platform or custom parsing configuration where required
fields.Payload Variations: Single event, batched events, raw endpoint, event endpoint, JSON payload, text payload, custom fields, source-defined timestamps and optional indexer acknowledgement
fields.Security Zone Use Case: The source can reach the approved HEC collector but cannot reach the final Splunk destination because of firewall policy, DMZ boundaries, security-zone restrictions or controlled egress
fields.Required Network Flows: Source zone → HEC collector on HTTPS; HEC collector → final Splunk destination using the approved forwarding protocol. Record firewall rule owner, source, destination, port, protocol and permitted direction.
fields.Default Health Profile: HEC listener availability, TLS status, token validity, HTTP response codes, acknowledgement latency, payload rejection, parsing quality, persistent queue, tcpout queue, onward forwarding, volume, event lag and end-to-end freshness
fields.Failure Behaviour: Return appropriate HEC errors, retry at the source where supported, use persistent queues on the collector, and alert on 4xx/5xx responses, invalid tokens, rejected payloads, blocked firewall flows, queue growth and stale downstream data
fields.Pattern Name: No add-on: HEC collector via Heavy Forwarder — Splunk on-premises
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise indexer or indexer cluster
fields.Destination Processing: Props/transforms and index-time routing on the approved parsing tier before indexing
fields.Destination Requirements: Approved receiving tier, certificates, indexes, sourcetypes, retention, licensing and infrastructure ownership
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow source systems to TCP 8088 or 443 on the Heavy Forwarder HEC listener; allow TCP 9997 to the receiving indexer cluster or approved Heavy Forwarder from the Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Restrict HEC ingress to approved source networks.
fields.Authentication Requirements: Use a dedicated HEC token on the Heavy Forwarder with least-privilege index access. Validate TLS and use client certificates/mutual TLS where required. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS trust to the final destination.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Provide the Heavy Forwarder HEC endpoint, token reference, event/raw endpoint, source IP allowlist, payload schema, timestamp, index, sourcetype, source and host metadata, batching limits, indexer acknowledgement setting and expected event volume.

definition: The source sends events directly to the Splunk Cloud HTTP Event Collector endpoint. No intermediary Heavy Forwarder is required.
relationshipRule: Source M:1 Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint. The source establishes direct HTTPS connectivity to Splunk Cloud and the events are indexed in approved Splunk Cloud indexes.
notes: Use where the source supports HEC or HTTPS event push, direct cloud connectivity is permitted, and no intermediary processing tier is required.

fields.Pattern Name: Direct HEC to Splunk Cloud
fields.Source Mechanism: Source-native HTTPS push to Splunk Cloud HEC
fields.HEC Configuration: Dedicated HEC token, approved index, source, sourcetype, TLS, optional channel, and indexer acknowledgement where supported
fields.Payload Variations: Single event, batched events, event endpoint, raw endpoint, JSON payload, text payload, custom fields, source-defined timestamps and optional acknowledgement
fields.Network Requirements: Source must have approved outbound HTTPS connectivity to the Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint. Apply DNS, proxy, certificate, allowlisting and firewall controls as required.
fields.Processing / Routing: HEC token metadata assignment, optional Ingest Processor routing, filtering, masking, enrichment, sourcetype assignment and index routing
fields.Default Health Profile: HEC endpoint availability, TLS validation, token validity, HTTP status codes, acknowledgement latency, payload rejection, ingestion lag, volume, parsing, required fields and end-to-end event freshness
fields.Failure Behaviour: Retry at the source where supported; alert on 4xx/5xx responses, token failure, TLS errors, DNS or proxy failure, rejected payloads, acknowledgement timeout and stale data
fields.Security Controls: Least-privilege HEC token, TLS certificate validation, restricted source access, approved indexes, token rotation, payload validation and monitoring of failed submissions
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow source systems outbound TCP 443 to https://<stack>.splunkcloud.com:443/services/collector or the stack-specific HEC hostname. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation, and restrict egress to the approved Splunk Cloud endpoint.
fields.Authentication Requirements: Use a dedicated Splunk Cloud HEC token with the minimum required index access. Validate the Splunk Cloud certificate; use a source-side secret store and rotate/revoke the token through the governed process.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Provide the Splunk Cloud stack/HEC FQDN, token reference, event or raw endpoint, index, sourcetype, source and host metadata, payload schema, timestamp format, batching and retry behaviour, and indexer acknowledgement setting where supported.

term: REST API polling via Azure Function → Splunk on-premises HEC
definition: No Splunk app or add-on is available and the source cannot push to HEC. A script running on Azure Function polls the source REST API, transforms the response and sends events to Splunk on-premises through HEC.
relationshipRule: Source REST API 1:M scripted polling executions on Azure Function; script M:1 Splunk on-premises HEC endpoint; final indexed destination is Splunk on-premises.
notes: Use where no supported app/add-on exists, the source only exposes a pull-based REST API, and a custom script is required to poll, checkpoint and forward data.

fields.Pattern Name: REST API polling via Azure Function → Splunk on-premises HEC
fields.Pattern Category: Custom REST API polling script to HEC
fields.Add-on / App Availability: No supported Splunk app or add-on is available
fields.Collection Direction: Pull from source; push to HEC
fields.Implementation Language: Python, PowerShell, C#, JavaScript or another supported Azure Functions runtime
fields.Source Authentication: OAuth 2.0, API key, token, certificate, service account or other source-supported authentication
fields.Runtime Identity / Secret Handling: Managed identity, Key Vault reference, OAuth client or API credential
fields.Polling Controls: Schedule, lookback window, checkpoint or cursor, pagination, rate-limit handling, backoff, retry, timeout, deduplication and idempotency
fields.Data Transformation: Validate schema, normalize records, split batches, set event time, source, sourcetype, host and custom fields, and remove or mask sensitive values
fields.HEC Delivery: HTTPS to Splunk on-premises HEC endpoint using a dedicated least-privilege HEC token; use batching and indexer acknowledgement where supported
fields.Payload Variations: Single event, batched events, JSON event endpoint, raw endpoint, text payload, custom fields, source-defined timestamps and optional acknowledgement
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise HEC receiver, indexer or Heavy Forwarder HEC tier
fields.Destination Processing: HEC token metadata assignment plus props/transforms, filtering, masking, enrichment, sourcetype assignment and index routing on the approved parsing tier
fields.Destination Requirements: Approved HEC receiver, token, TLS certificate, index, source, sourcetype, retention, licensing and infrastructure ownership
fields.Network Requirements: Azure Function must reach the source REST API and the selected HEC endpoint through approved outbound routes, private endpoints, proxy or firewall rules as required
fields.Security Zone Considerations: Document source API zone, script runtime zone and HEC destination zone. Permit only required outbound API and HEC flows, apply TLS validation, proxy controls and least-privilege firewall rules.
fields.Checkpoint / State Store: Use durable state such as Azure Storage, DynamoDB/S3, local protected state, KV store or another reliable checkpoint store appropriate to the runtime
fields.Default Health Profile: Scheduler or invocation success, source API availability, authentication, pagination completion, checkpoint age, rate-limit events, script duration, record counts, duplicate rate, HEC availability, HTTP status codes, acknowledgement latency, payload rejection and end-to-end event freshness
fields.Runtime-Specific Health: Function invocation success, timer execution, cold-start or timeout failures, dependency errors, Application Insights failures and function retry status
fields.Failure Behaviour: Retry with exponential backoff, preserve checkpoints only after successful delivery, send failed batches to a dead-letter or quarantine path where available, and alert on stale checkpoints, repeated API failures, throttling, HEC errors, rejected payloads and missing downstream events
fields.Operational Ownership: Integration team owns the script and API contract; platform team owns HEC, indexes, sourcetypes and destination health
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 from the runtime to the source REST API and allow TCP 8088 to the Splunk Enterprise HEC endpoint, or TCP 443 when published through an approved load balancer or reverse proxy. Permit DNS, TLS certificate validation and identity/secret-service endpoints. Where VNet integration is used, add the required NSG, route, NAT, proxy or private-endpoint rules for both the source API and HEC.
fields.Authentication Requirements: Configure the source API credential required by the vendor, such as OAuth 2.0 client credentials, API key, bearer token, certificate or service username/password, plus a dedicated least-privilege HEC token for delivery. Use a managed identity or service principal for Azure resources, and store source and HEC secrets in Azure Key Vault or protected application settings.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Provide source API base URL and region, tenant/account/organisation ID where applicable, endpoint paths and datasets, polling schedule, lookback window, pagination/cursor, checkpoint key, rate limits, retry rules, payload schema, event timestamp and target index/sourcetype. Also provide Azure subscription ID, resource group, Function App name, region, storage account, managed identity/service principal, Key Vault reference, VNet/subnet and timer-trigger schedule.

term: Syslog server with forwarder collection — Splunk on-premises
definition: Sources send syslog to an intermediary syslog server. The server writes events to files, a Splunk forwarder monitors those files, and events are forwarded to Splunk Enterprise.
relationshipRule: Source M:1 syslog server; syslog server 1:1 or 1:M forwarder; forwarder M:1 Splunk Enterprise.
notes: Use when sources send to a local syslog collector and the forwarder provides the controlled path to on-premises indexers.

fields.Pattern Category: Syslog server with forwarder file collection
fields.Source Mechanism: Source sends syslog to a syslog server
fields.Collection Direction: Push to syslog server; forwarder monitors written files
fields.Intermediate Storage: Syslog server writes events to controlled files/directories
fields.Forwarder Collection: Splunk Universal Forwarder on the syslog server monitors the files; use a Heavy Forwarder instead where local parsing, routing or app execution is required
fields.Required App / TA: Vendor TA or custom parsing where available; generic syslog otherwise
fields.Processing / Routing: Listener rules, file naming, metadata assignment, line breaking, timestamp extraction, props/transforms, filtering, masking and onward forwarding
fields.File Management: File permissions, rotation, retention, compression, inode handling, archive exclusion and forwarder read position
fields.Security Zone Use Case: Use where sources may send only to an approved syslog collector in their zone and the forwarder provides controlled onward connectivity
fields.Required Network Flows: Source → syslog server on approved syslog port; forwarder → final Splunk destination using approved TLS forwarding
fields.Default Health Profile: Listener status, incoming traffic, file creation/growth, disk usage, rotation health, forwarder heartbeat, monitor activity, queue health, forwarding success, parsing quality, volume and end-to-end freshness
fields.Failure Behaviour: Alert on listener failure, firewall denies, missing traffic, disk pressure, stalled files, rotation errors, forwarder disconnects, queue growth and stale downstream data
fields.Pattern Name: Syslog server with forwarder collection — Splunk on-premises
fields.Destination Platform: Splunk Enterprise indexer or indexer cluster
fields.Destination Processing: Props/transforms and index-time routing on the approved parsing tier before indexing
fields.Port / Firewall Requirements: Allow source devices to the syslog server on UDP/TCP 514 or TCP 6514 for TLS; allow TCP 9997 to the receiving indexer cluster or approved Heavy Forwarder from the Universal or Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Restrict listeners to approved source networks.
fields.Authentication Requirements: UDP/TCP syslog normally has no application credential. Use server certificates and optional mutual TLS for TLS syslog. The forwarder service account requires read access to the written files, and Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust.
fields.Source Platform Requirements: Provide each source hostname/IP, vendor/product, target syslog server, protocol/port, facility/severity and message format. Define syslog listener rules, output file paths, ownership/permissions, rotation/retention/compression, forwarder monitor stanzas, host metadata, index, sourcetype and expected EPS.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Runtime Availability • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable runtime-assurance control for custom REST polling or event-processing code executed in Azure Functions. Replace resource identifiers, metric names and thresholds with approved implementation values.

fields.Test Description: Confirm the Function App is running and every required function remains enabled.
fields.Pass Criteria: The Function App state is Running and all required functions are enabled.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and start or re-enable the affected application or function.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<azure_monitor_index> resource_type="MICROSOFT.WEB/SITES" earliest=-15m | stats latest(app_state) as app_state latest(function_enabled) as function_enabled by subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name | lookup expected_azure_functions subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name OUTPUT status | where status="active" AND (app_state!="Running" OR function_enabled!=1)
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Trigger Health • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable runtime-assurance control for custom REST polling or event-processing code executed in Azure Functions. Replace resource identifiers, metric names and thresholds with approved implementation values.

fields.Test Description: Confirm timer, Event Hub, queue, HTTP or other approved triggers invoke the function within the expected interval.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every active function has a successful invocation within its trigger-specific interval.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and investigate trigger configuration, schedule, event source or runtime state.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): | inputlookup expected_azure_functions | where status="active" | join type=left subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name [ search index=<azure_function_log_index> earliest=-24h invocation_status="Success" | stats max(_time) as last_success by subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name ] | eval age=now()-last_success | where isnull(last_success) OR age>expected_interval_seconds
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Execution Reliability • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable runtime-assurance control for custom REST polling or event-processing code executed in Azure Functions. Replace resource identifiers, metric names and thresholds with approved implementation values.

fields.Test Description: Monitor failed, cancelled and unhandled-exception invocations.
fields.Pass Criteria: Failure percentage remains below the approved warning threshold with no sustained failure sequence.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 for sustained failure and P2 for warning-level error rate.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<azure_function_log_index> earliest=-15m | stats count as total count(eval(invocation_status!="Success")) as failed by function_app function_name | eval failure_pct=100*failed/total | where failure_pct>=<warning_failure_pct>
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Performance • High
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable runtime-assurance control for custom REST polling or event-processing code executed in Azure Functions. Replace resource identifiers, metric names and thresholds with approved implementation values.

fields.Test Description: Detect slow executions, timeouts and duration growth relative to the configured function timeout.
fields.Pass Criteria: p95 duration remains below the warning limit and no invocation reaches the hard timeout.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P2 and optimise code, dependencies, plan sizing or timeout configuration.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<azure_function_log_index> earliest=-1h | stats perc95(duration_ms) as p95_duration max(duration_ms) as max_duration count(eval(result="Timeout")) as timeouts by function_app function_name | lookup expected_azure_functions function_app function_name OUTPUT warning_duration_ms timeout_ms | where p95_duration>warning_duration_ms OR max_duration>=timeout_ms OR timeouts>0
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Resource Capacity • Critical

fields.Test Name: Memory, CPU and Host Resource Pressure

fields.Pass Criteria: No OOM or worker restart occurs and resource use remains below approved limits.

fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

fields.Test Description: Confirm Azure Storage, Cosmos DB or other approved state store is accessible and checkpoints advance safely.

fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.

definition: Azure Function Runtime • Recovery • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01

fields.Test Name: Retry, Poison Message and Replay Backlog
fields.Test Description: Monitor retry counts, poison queues, dead-letter storage and replay backlog for failed records.
fields.Pass Criteria: Retry rates remain within baseline and poison/replay backlogs are empty or draining within SLA.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 for growing backlog and P2 for isolated retry anomalies.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<azure_function_log_index> earliest=-1h event_type IN ("retry","poison_message","dead_letter","replay") | stats sum(retry_count) as retries sum(backlog_count) as backlog max(oldest_age_seconds) as oldest_age by function_app function_name queue_name | where backlog><warning_backlog> OR oldest_age><max_oldest_age_seconds> OR retries><max_retries>
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Retry or replay backlog beyond threshold
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

fields.Test Description: Validate runtime version, deployment package or slot, application settings hash and infrastructure assignment against the approved baseline.

fields.Failure Action: Alert P2 and redeploy, patch or correct the non-compliant Function App.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<azure_function_inventory_index> earliest=-24h | stats latest(runtime_version) as runtime_version latest(deployment_hash) as deployment_hash latest(settings_hash) as settings_hash latest(slot) as slot by subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name | lookup approved_azure_function_baseline subscription_id resource_group function_app function_name OUTPUT approved_runtime approved_deployment_hash approved_settings_hash approved_slot | where runtime_version!=approved_runtime OR deployment_hash!=approved_deployment_hash OR settings_hash!=approved_settings_hash OR slot!=approved_slot
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Functions not matching approved runtime or deployment
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Azure Function inventory containing subscription ID, tenant ID, resource group, Function App, function name, trigger type, schedule, hosting plan, runtime version, managed identity, VNet, storage account, secret references, destination endpoint and approved deployment/configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Azure Monitor FunctionAppLogs, AppServiceConsoleLogs, platform metrics, Application Insights traces, dependency results, storage/checkpoint telemetry, managed-identity failures and deployment metadata.

definition: Heavy Forwarder Platform / Intermediary • Service Health • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable Heavy Forwarder platform and intermediary assurance control. Applies where a Heavy Forwarder receives, parses, transforms, routes or relays data between security zones or into Splunk Cloud/on-premises destinations.

fields.Test Description: Confirm splunkd is running, responsive and configured to start automatically on every expected Heavy Forwarder.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every active Heavy Forwarder reports a running and enabled splunkd service within the heartbeat interval.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and restart or repair the Heavy Forwarder service.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<hf_telemetry_index> event_type=service_state service_name=splunkd earliest=-15m | stats latest(state) as state latest(startup) as startup latest(_time) as last_seen by host | lookup expected_heavy_forwarders hf_host AS host OUTPUT status | where status="active" AND (state!="running" OR startup NOT IN ("enabled","automatic") OR now()-last_seen>900)
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Heavy Forwarders with stopped, disabled or stale service
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Heavy Forwarder inventory containing node, pool, role, region or security zone, management port, receiving listeners, upstream source groups, downstream destinations, persistent queue paths, deployment server or configuration manager assignment, installed apps and versions, approved configuration hash, TLS certificates, service account, resource thresholds and expected throughput.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect Heavy Forwarder splunkd, metrics.log, introspection, deployment-client, configuration-tracker, queue, tcpin/tcpout, parsing, resource, TLS, crash and destination-connectivity telemetry, plus source-to-destination reconciliation metrics where available.

definition: Heavy Forwarder Platform / Intermediary • Operational Recovery • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01

fields.Test Name: Crash, Restart, Pending Restart and Recovery
fields.Test Description: Detect crashes, repeated restarts, pending restart requirements, unclean shutdowns and failure to replay queued data after recovery.
fields.Pass Criteria: No unexpected crash or restart loop exists, required restarts are completed within SLA, and queued data drains after recovery.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 for crash loops or failed recovery and P2 for overdue pending restart.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd earliest=-1h ("crash" OR "unclean shutdown" OR "restart required" OR "Splunkd starting" OR "queue recovery") | stats count(eval(match(_raw,"crash|unclean"))) as crashes count(eval(match(_raw,"Splunkd starting"))) as starts max(eval(if(match(_raw,"restart required"),_time,null()))) as restart_required_time latest(eval(if(match(_raw,"queue recovery"),recovery_status,null()))) as recovery_status by host | where crashes>0 OR starts><max_starts_per_hour> OR (isnotnull(restart_required_time) AND now()-restart_required_time><restart_sla_seconds>) OR recovery_status="failed"
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Hosts with crash, restart-loop, overdue restart or failed recovery
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Heavy Forwarder inventory containing node, pool, role, region or security zone, management port, receiving listeners, upstream source groups, downstream destinations, persistent queue paths, deployment server or configuration manager assignment, installed apps and versions, approved configuration hash, TLS certificates, service account, resource thresholds and expected throughput.

fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Required functions unavailable or wrong alias version
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative AWS Lambda inventory containing account ID, region, function ARN, alias/version, trigger or event-source mapping, schedule, runtime, architecture, memory, timeout, reserved concurrency, execution role, VPC/subnets/security groups, environment/settings hash, secret references and destinations.

fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative AWS Lambda inventory containing account ID, region, function ARN, alias/version, trigger or event-source mapping, schedule, runtime, architecture, memory, timeout, reserved concurrency, execution role, VPC/subnets/security groups, environment/settings hash, secret references and destinations.

fields.Test Description: Detect expected active hosts that have produced no events for the governed input.

fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): | inputlookup expected_input_hosts | where input_id="<input_id>" AND lifecycle_status="active" | rename expected_host as host | eval expected=1 | join type=left host [ search index=<index> sourcetype=<sourcetype> earliest=-<lookback> | stats max(_time) as last_event count as event_count by host ] | eval age_seconds=now()-last_event | where isnull(last_event) OR age_seconds><critical_seconds>

fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=_internal source=*metrics.log group=tcpin_connections earliest=-30m | stats max(_time) as last_connection by hostname | rename hostname as host | join type=left host [ search index=<index> sourcetype=<sourcetype> earliest=-30m | stats max(_time) as last_data count as data_count by host ] | where isnotnull(last_connection) AND (isnull(last_data) OR now()-last_data><critical_seconds>)

definition: osquery • Agent Health • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable osquery input-assurance control. Replace index, sourcetype, host, query, pack, manager and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. Collect status/configuration telemetry through the approved osquery manager or local administration channel; never place enrolment secrets or private keys in SPL.

fields.Test Description: Confirm the osquery service or daemon is installed, running and configured for automatic restart on every expected host.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every expected host reports a running osquery service or daemon within the allowed heartbeat window.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and restore the osquery service or daemon
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): | inputlookup expected_osquery_hosts | where status="active" | rename expected_host as host | join type=left host [ search index=<osquery_telemetry_index> earliest=-15m event_type=osquery_service_state | stats latest(service_state) as service_state max(_time) as last_state by host ] | eval age=now()-last_state | where isnull(last_state) OR service_state!="running" OR age>900
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Hosts with stopped or stale osquery service
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative osquery inventory containing expected hosts, platform, agent version, node key, enrolment state, assigned packs, expected query intervals, required tables and approved configuration hash.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect osquery status logs, result logs, scheduled-query metadata, service state, configuration hash, enrolment/backend state, database metrics and forwarding telemetry into searchable Splunk indexes.

fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative osquery inventory containing expected hosts, platform, agent version, node key, enrolment state, assigned packs, expected query intervals, required tables and approved configuration hash.

fields.Test Name: Host Identity and Node Key Consistency
fields.Test Description: Detect node-key reuse, host identity changes and multiple active agents claiming the same stable identity.
fields.Pass Criteria: Each active node key maps to one approved host identity and each host maps to one active node key unless explicitly re-enrolled.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and investigate cloned images, duplicate enrolment or identity corruption
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<osquery_index> earliest=-24h | stats dc(host) as hosts values(host) as host_values dc(node_key) as node_keys values(node_key) as node_key_values by machine_uuid | where hosts>1 OR node_keys>1 | append [ search index=<osquery_index> earliest=-24h | stats dc(machine_uuid) as machine_uuids values(machine_uuid) as values by node_key | where machine_uuids>1 ]
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative osquery inventory containing expected hosts, platform, agent version, node key, enrolment state, assigned packs, expected query intervals, required tables and approved configuration hash.

relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable REST API and custom-script resilience control. Replace input, telemetry index, API, runtime, checkpoint, source-key and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. Requires per-run collection telemetry, checkpoint state, HTTP response metadata, delivery acknowledgements and replay-queue metrics to be searchable.

fields.Test Description: Confirm each REST collection run follows all pages or continuation tokens through the final page without silently stopping early.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every completed run reaches the terminal page/token and reports no unresolved continuation token.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and hold checkpoint advancement
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h event_type=collection_run | stats latest(run_status) as run_status latest(final_page_reached) as final_page_reached latest(next_token) as next_token by input_id run_id | where run_status="success" AND (final_page_reached!=1 OR isnotnull(next_token))
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

definition: REST API / Custom Script • Completeness • Critical

fields.Test Description: Reconcile records received and delivered with the total count, page counts or source-side export count reported by the API.
fields.Pass Criteria: Collected and delivered record counts match the authoritative API total within the approved tolerance.
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h event_type=collection_summary | eval missing=coalesce(api_total,records_received)-records_delivered | eval variance_pct=round(100*abs(missing)/max(coalesce(api_total,records_received),1),2) | where missing!=0 AND variance_pct><allowed_variance_pct>
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

fields.Test Description: Ensure the collection checkpoint advances only after all records for the checkpoint window have been accepted by the destination.
fields.Pass Criteria: No checkpoint advancement occurs for failed, partial or unacknowledged delivery runs.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1, freeze input and preserve replay state
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h event_type=checkpoint_update | stats latest(checkpoint_before) as before latest(checkpoint_after) as after latest(delivery_status) as delivery_status latest(delivery_ack) as delivery_ack by input_id run_id | where after>before AND (delivery_status!="success" OR delivery_ack!=1)
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

fields.Test Description: Detect checkpoints moving backwards, resetting unexpectedly or jumping beyond the last confirmed source position.

fields.Failure Action: Alert P2 and review for duplicate or skipped data
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-24h event_type=checkpoint_update | sort 0 input_id _time | streamstats current=f last(checkpoint_after) as previous_checkpoint by input_id | eval delta=checkpoint_after-previous_checkpoint | where isnotnull(previous_checkpoint) AND (delta<0 OR delta><max_checkpoint_jump>)
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h event_type=retry | sort 0 input_id run_id attempt | streamstats current=f last(_time) as previous_retry by input_id run_id | eval retry_delay=_time-previous_retry | where attempt><max_retry_attempts> OR (attempt>1 AND retry_delay<<minimum_backoff_seconds>)

fields.Test Description: Confirm HTTP 429 responses and provider throttling signals honour Retry-After or the approved provider-specific backoff interval.
fields.Pass Criteria: No request is retried before the provider Retry-After interval and throttled runs recover without data loss.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P2 and reduce concurrency/request rate
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h (http_status=429 OR throttled=1) | eval required_wait=coalesce(retry_after_seconds,<default_backoff_seconds>) | eval actual_wait=next_request_time-_time | where actual_wait<required_wait OR recovery_status="failed"
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

fields.Test Name: Partial or Truncated API Response Rejection
fields.Test Description: Ensure incomplete HTTP bodies, content-length mismatches, invalid decompression, malformed JSON/XML and interrupted streams are rejected rather than checkpointed as successful.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every accepted response passes transport-length, decompression and payload-parse validation.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1, reject response and retain prior checkpoint
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-2h event_type=response_validation | where accepted=1 AND (body_complete!=1 OR content_length_match!=1 OR decompression_ok!=1 OR payload_parse_ok!=1)

fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and initiate controlled replay
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-24h event_type=replay_queue | stats latest(queue_depth) as queue_depth latest(oldest_record_age_seconds) as oldest_age latest(unrecoverable_count) as unrecoverable by input_id | where unrecoverable>0 OR queue_depth><max_replay_queue_depth> OR oldest_age><max_replay_age_seconds>

fields.Test Description: Validate the script runtime can load required modules, resolve DNS, access its secret store and obtain usable credentials before collection starts.
fields.Pass Criteria: All runtime dependency, DNS, secret retrieval and credential preflight checks succeed.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P2 and prevent collection run from advancing state
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<collector_telemetry_index> input_id=<input_id> earliest=-30m event_type=runtime_preflight | stats latest(module_check) as module_check latest(dns_check) as dns_check latest(secret_access) as secret_access latest(credential_valid) as credential_valid latest(_time) as last_check by input_id runtime_id | eval age=now()-last_check | where module_check!="pass" OR dns_check!="pass" OR secret_access!="pass" OR credential_valid!="pass" OR age>1800
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Failed or stale runtime preflight checks
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Per-run start/end/status, page and continuation-token state, API-reported totals, records received/delivered/rejected, checkpoint before/after, HTTP status and Retry-After, retry attempts, response validation, schema/version fingerprint, delivery acknowledgement, replay/dead-letter queue state, runtime dependency and secret-access preflight results.

definition: Raw TCP Input • Input Configuration • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable non-syslog raw TCP input-assurance control. Replace listener, port, source, index, sourcetype, framing and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. TLS checks are conditional.

fields.Test Description: Confirm the approved non-syslog TCP input stanza is enabled on the intended Splunk receiver.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every approved raw TCP input is enabled on the expected receiver and port.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and restore or correct the input stanza
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): | rest /services/data/inputs/tcp/raw | search disabled=0 | eval listener=host.":".port | lookup expected_raw_tcp_inputs listener OUTPUT listener AS expected_listener | where isnull(expected_listener)
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Missing or unexpected enabled raw TCP inputs
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative raw-TCP input inventory containing listener host, port, bind address, expected source IPs, TLS requirement, framing method, maximum event size, approved index, sourcetype and expected traffic profile.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect splunkd listener, connection, queue, throughput, parsing, TLS and routing telemetry, plus synthetic connectivity results where permitted.

definition: Raw TCP Input • Listener Availability • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable non-syslog raw TCP input-assurance control. Replace listener, port, source, index, sourcetype, framing and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. TLS checks are conditional.

fields.Test Description: Verify splunkd has successfully bound the configured raw TCP listener port without address-in-use or permission errors.
fields.Pass Criteria: The configured listener is bound and no recent bind errors exist.

fields.Test Description: Confirm every expected Splunk Stream sensor or streamfwd instance is active and reporting telemetry.

fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<stream_internal_index> component=streamfwd earliest=-15m | stats max(_time) as last_heartbeat by sensor_id host | eval age=now()-last_heartbeat | lookup expected_stream_sensors sensor_id OUTPUT lifecycle_status expected_interval_seconds | where lifecycle_status="active" AND (isnull(last_heartbeat) OR age>2*expected_interval_seconds)
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Authoritative expected_stream_sensors, expected_stream_coverage, expected_stream_protocols and approved_stream_configs lookups keyed by sensor, interface, stream and protocol; include lifecycle state, expected interval, approved version/config, index and sourcetype.

definition: Sysmon • Agent Health • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable Sysmon input-assurance control. Replace index, sourcetype, host, Event ID, configuration and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. Requirements must be role-aware because not every Sysmon Event ID is enabled on every host.

fields.Test Description: Confirm the Sysmon service is installed, running and configured to start automatically on every expected host.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every expected host reports a running Sysmon service within the approved telemetry interval.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and restore the Sysmon service
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): | inputlookup expected_sysmon_hosts | where status="active" | rename expected_host as host | join type=left host [ search index=<windows_telemetry_index> earliest=-15m event_type=sysmon_service_state | stats latest(service_state) as service_state max(_time) as last_state by host ] | eval age=now()-last_state | where isnull(last_state) OR service_state!="running" OR age>900
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Hosts with stopped or stale Sysmon service
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Sysmon inventory containing expected hosts, host roles, required Event IDs, approved Sysmon version, service/driver state, configuration hash, channel settings and routing requirements.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect the Sysmon Operational channel plus service, driver, configuration, EventRecordID, channel-retention and Splunk routing telemetry for every expected host.

fields.Test Description: Verify the Sysmon kernel driver is loaded, running and matches the approved driver/service pair.
fields.Pass Criteria: Every expected host reports a loaded, running and approved Sysmon driver.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and repair the Sysmon installation or driver state
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<windows_telemetry_index> earliest=-15m event_type=sysmon_driver_state | stats latest(driver_state) as driver_state latest(driver_name) as driver_name latest(driver_version) as driver_version max(_time) as last_state by host | lookup expected_sysmon_hosts expected_host AS host OUTPUT approved_driver_name approved_driver_version | where driver_state!="running" OR driver_name!=approved_driver_name OR driver_version!=approved_driver_version OR now()-last_state>900
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Hosts with missing or non-compliant Sysmon driver
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Sysmon inventory containing expected hosts, host roles, required Event IDs, approved Sysmon version, service/driver state, configuration hash, channel settings and routing requirements.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect the Sysmon Operational channel plus service, driver, configuration, EventRecordID, channel-retention and Splunk routing telemetry for every expected host.

fields.Test Name: Service Stop Uninstall or Driver Error
fields.Test Description: Detect Sysmon service stops, uninstall activity, driver load failures and fatal operational-channel errors.
fields.Pass Criteria: No unapproved stop, uninstall or driver failure occurs on an expected host.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 to SOC and Windows Engineering
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): (index=<sysmon_index> earliest=-15m (EventID=4 OR event_id=4) message="*stopped*") OR (index=<windows_index> earliest=-15m (source="Service Control Manager" OR Provider_Name="Service Control Manager") message="*Sysmon*" (message="*stopped*" OR message="*deleted*" OR message="*failed*")) | stats count values(message) as messages by host
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Sysmon stop, uninstall or driver error events

fields.Test Description: Detect unexpected EventRecordID resets, gaps, channel clearing, undersized channel capacity or overwrite behaviour inconsistent with policy.
fields.Pass Criteria: EventRecordID progression is explainable and channel retention settings meet the approved policy.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 for unexplained reset/clear and P2 for retention drift
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<sysmon_index> earliest=-1h | sort 0 host _time | streamstats current=f last(EventRecordID) as previous_id by host | eval gap=EventRecordID-previous_id | stats count(eval(gap<0)) as resets max(gap) as max_gap by host | join type=left host [ search index=<windows_telemetry_index> earliest=-24h event_type=windows_channel_state channel="Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" | stats latest(max_size_mb) as max_size_mb latest(retention_mode) as retention_mode by host ] | lookup expected_sysmon_hosts expected_host AS host OUTPUT minimum_channel_size_mb approved_retention_mode | where resets>0 OR max_gap><max_record_gap> OR max_size_mb<minimum_channel_size_mb OR retention_mode!=approved_retention_mode
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Hosts with continuity or retention failure
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Sysmon inventory containing expected hosts, host roles, required Event IDs, approved Sysmon version, service/driver state, configuration hash, channel settings and routing requirements.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect the Sysmon Operational channel plus service, driver, configuration, EventRecordID, channel-retention and Splunk routing telemetry for every expected host.

fields.Test Description: Validate required Sysmon fields are extracted for each Event ID and detect XML/schema parsing regressions.
fields.Pass Criteria: Required fields meet the approved completeness threshold for every monitored Event ID.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 when detection-critical fields are missing and P2 for other extraction regressions
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<sysmon_index> earliest=-1h | eval missing_process=if(EventID=1 AND (isnull(Image) OR isnull(ProcessGuid) OR isnull(CommandLine)),1,0), missing_network=if(EventID=3 AND (isnull(SourceIp) OR isnull(DestinationIp) OR isnull(DestinationPort)),1,0), missing_dns=if(EventID=22 AND isnull(QueryName),1,0) | stats count as total sum(missing_process) as missing_process sum(missing_network) as missing_network sum(missing_dns) as missing_dns by EventID sourcetype | eval missing_pct=100*(missing_process+missing_network+missing_dns)/total | where missing_pct><max_missing_field_pct>
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Event IDs with missing required fields
fields.Definition: Inventory Requirement: Maintain an authoritative Sysmon inventory containing expected hosts, host roles, required Event IDs, approved Sysmon version, service/driver state, configuration hash, channel settings and routing requirements.
fields.Definition: Telemetry Requirement: Collect the Sysmon Operational channel plus service, driver, configuration, EventRecordID, channel-retention and Splunk routing telemetry for every expected host.

definition: Sysmon • Timestamp Quality • Critical
relationshipRule: Current health test template classified under TAX-04.07.01
sourceWorksheet: Input Test Catalog / Health Test Definitions
notes: Reusable Sysmon input-assurance control. Replace index, sourcetype, host, Event ID, configuration and threshold placeholders with approved implementation values. Requirements must be role-aware because not every Sysmon Event ID is enabled on every host.

fields.Test Description: Detect future or delayed Sysmon timestamps and mismatches between Splunk host, Computer and stable host identity.
fields.Pass Criteria: Timestamp skew remains within tolerance and event host attribution matches the approved computer identity.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 for identity mismatch and P2 for clock or timestamp failure
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<sysmon_index> earliest=-1h | eval delta=_time-_indextime, event_host=lower(mvindex(split(coalesce(Computer,ComputerName),"."),0)), splunk_host=lower(mvindex(split(host,"."),0)) | stats median(delta) as median_delta max(abs(delta)) as max_abs_delta count(eval(event_host!=splunk_host)) as identity_mismatches by host | where abs(median_delta)><max_clock_skew_seconds> OR identity_mismatches>0

fields.Test Description: Ensure the Splunk host value represents the originating Windows computer rather than the collector, deployment server or a placeholder.
fields.Pass Criteria: Splunk host matches the normalised Windows computer identity for every event, subject to approved alias mappings.
fields.Failure Action: Alert P1 and correct host attribution before downstream detections are affected
fields.Definition: SPL Query (truncated): index=<windows_index> earliest=-1h | eval windows_computer=mvindex(split(lower(coalesce(ComputerName,Computer,Hostname)),"."),0), splunk_host=mvindex(split(lower(host),"."),0) | lookup approved_host_aliases observed_host AS splunk_host OUTPUT canonical_host | eval expected_host=coalesce(canonical_host,windows_computer) | where isnull(windows_computer) OR splunk_host IN ("localhost","unknown","-") OR splunk_host!=expected_host | stats count values(windows_computer) as windows_computers by host sourcetype
fields.Definition: Threshold Type: Incorrect or placeholder Windows host attribution
