definition: Governed patterns for registry identifiers, Splunk technical objects, health checks, detection content and analytical assets.
mandatoryAttributes: Object type; pattern; separator; case; example; owner; exception process
relationshipRule: Applies across all governed taxonomy entities and Splunk objects

definition: Defines approved platform architecture, configuration and operating requirements.
mandatoryAttributes: Standard; scope; owner; version; status
relationshipRule: A platform may reference one or more applicable platform standards.

definition: Defines approved event logging, timestamp, field, retention and monitoring requirements.
mandatoryAttributes: Standard; scope; owner; version; status
relationshipRule: A platform, system or logging integration may reference one or more logging standards.

definition: Defines the approved minimum configuration or secure baseline for a platform or logging component.
mandatoryAttributes: Baseline; version; owner; compliance status
relationshipRule: A platform or component may reference one or more approved configuration baselines.

definition: Defines datasets, reusable collection patterns, collection components and routing into Splunk.
mandatoryAttributes: Domain name; steward; status
relationshipRule: Root domain

definition: Groups the source, its input mapping and its intended data destination.
mandatoryAttributes: Data Source; source-input mapping; destination
relationshipRule: A data source has one or more collection mappings and approved destinations.

definition: Defines approved logging patterns, transports, routing, implemented collection topologies and the support status of each collection path.
mandatoryAttributes: Logging pattern; transport; collection routing; implemented topology; collection path support status
relationshipRule: Each onboarded source should use an approved logging pattern and document the implemented topology, transport and route. Deviations from the approved pattern must be identified.

definition: Groups deployed components that collect, receive, forward or process log data.
mandatoryAttributes: Component type; component name; owner; status
relationshipRule: A collection architecture may contain one or more collection components.

definition: Defines configuration that controls how event data is enabled at the source, collected, polled, received, checkpointed, retried and presented to the collection component.
mandatoryAttributes: Input stanza or source-side configuration; parameters; schedule or trigger; state handling; retry behaviour where applicable
relationshipRule: Collection components should have documented, reviewable configuration linked to their source and logging pattern.

definition: Defines source-specific parameters required by the input, such as endpoint, tenant, subscription, bucket, namespace, path or query.
mandatoryAttributes: Parameter name; value reference; source; component; owner
relationshipRule: Input parameters belong to an input configuration and should avoid storing secrets directly.
notes: Secret values remain under Data Collection Authentication and approved secret stores.

definition: Defines how frequently a pull-based collector or scripted input polls the source.
mandatoryAttributes: Interval; unit; source; component; rationale
relationshipRule: Polling interval should match source availability, API limits, latency requirements and volume expectations.

definition: Defines batching, cursor, offset, watermark or checkpoint state used to prevent event loss or duplication.
mandatoryAttributes: Checkpoint type; storage location; reset procedure; owner
relationshipRule: Pull-based and stream-based collection should document durable state and recovery behaviour.

definition: Defines retry limits, backoff, timeout and dead-letter behaviour for collection failures.
mandatoryAttributes: Retry count; backoff; timeout; failure action; alerting
relationshipRule: Collection retries should avoid data loss, uncontrolled duplication and source API overload.

definition: Defines the configuration applied on the source system, appliance, application or service to enable, select, format and transmit the required events before they reach a collector or Splunk component.
mandatoryAttributes: Source system; configuration scope; enabled log categories; destination; transport; format; change reference; owner; validation status
relationshipRule: A data source may have one or more source-side logging configurations. Each configuration should reference the affected source, approved collection topology and downstream input configuration.
notes: Examples include FortiGate log filters and policy logging, Windows audit policy, application audit settings, SaaS export configuration and cloud diagnostic settings. Do not duplicate Splunk-side inputs.conf content here.

definition: Defines a logical source of security, operational or audit data that is collected for SIEM use.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; Data Source Name; Data Format; Sourcetype; Index; Owner; Criticality; Status
relationshipRule: Platform 1:M Data Sources
notes: Includes reference source-family catalogue entries and future operational Data Source records.

definition: Defines the approved end-to-end collection architecture used to move data from a source to its destination.
mandatoryAttributes: Pattern Name; Category; Source Mechanism; Collection Tier; Transport; Destination; Health Profile
relationshipRule: Logging Pattern 1:M Data Source Input Mappings

definition: Maps a data source to the collection input, component, route and destination used to ingest its events.
mandatoryAttributes: Data Source ID; Component ID; Logging Pattern ID; Collection Role; Status
relationshipRule: Data Sources M:M Input Components

definition: Defines a deployed component that receives, polls, forwards or processes source data.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; Input Type; App or TA; Collector; Sourcetype; Index; Owner; Status
relationshipRule: Platform 1:M Input Components; input components may feed collectors, Ingest Processor pipelines, index destinations or routing tiers.

definition: Defines the collector instance or service responsible for receiving or retrieving data.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; Collector Type; Hostname; Region; Status
relationshipRule: Input Component M:1 Collector

definition: Defines the configured input stanza and its collection-specific parameters.
mandatoryAttributes: Stanza name; input component; collector; transport; source; index; sourcetype reference; status
relationshipRule: Input Component 1:M input stanzas; parsing stanzas are governed under TAX-04

definition: Defines the Splunk app, add-on or integration package used to support collection and normalisation.
mandatoryAttributes: App Name; Version; Vendor; Platform; Purpose; Owner; Status
relationshipRule: App or TA M:M Components
notes: Compatibility with source product, firmware and Splunk versions is recorded under TAX-03.03.03.01.

definition: Records compatibility between the source product or firmware version, the Splunk app or technology add-on version, the supported Splunk platform version and the expected parsing or sourcetype behaviour.
mandatoryAttributes: Vendor; product; source version; app or add-on name; app or add-on version; Splunk version; support status; expected sourcetypes; validation evidence
relationshipRule: An app or technology add-on may have multiple compatibility records covering different product, firmware and Splunk platform versions.
notes: Use this to capture changes such as legacy versus current sourcetype prefixes, supported FortiOS releases, CIM compatibility and vendor support statements.

definition: Defines the protocol, port, network path and delivery mechanism used to transport collected data.
mandatoryAttributes: Protocol; port; encryption; authentication
relationshipRule: One or more transport definitions per pattern

definition: Defines the required delivery reliability, loss tolerance, acknowledgement, ordering, retry and encryption characteristics for the transport used by the collection path.
mandatoryAttributes: Transport reference; reliability classification; loss tolerance; acknowledgement requirement; retry or buffering requirement; ordering requirement; encryption requirement; rationale
relationshipRule: Each transport used in a collection topology may have one or more reliability requirements based on event criticality and operational risk.
notes: Examples: UDP loss accepted for low-value telemetry; TCP required; TLS required; HEC acknowledgements required; local disk buffering required; guaranteed delivery not available.

definition: Defines routing decisions and pipeline paths applied before data reaches its final destination.
mandatoryAttributes: Pattern ID; route name; source; condition; destination; status
relationshipRule: Logging Pattern 1:M collection routing rules; Ingest Processor routing belongs here while event-structure processing is governed under TAX-04.

definition: Defines the target Splunk index or other approved storage destination for collected data.
mandatoryAttributes: Index name; retention; access; destination type
relationshipRule: Data Source M:M Index Destinations

definition: Defines an Azure Function used as a scripted or serverless data collection component.
mandatoryAttributes: Function App; trigger; authentication; source API; destination; owner; status
relationshipRule: Azure Function M:1 Data Source; Azure Function M:1 HEC endpoint or processing pipeline
notes: Cloud-hosted PaaS collection and transformation component.

definition: Defines sourcetype identity, event structure, timestamp handling, parsing, field normalisation, event behaviour, health checks and scored data-quality assessments.
mandatoryAttributes: Domain name; steward; status
relationshipRule: Root domain

definition: Granular event type contained within a data source or sourcetype.
mandatoryAttributes: Data Source ID; Platform ID; Event Name; Identifier; Sourcetype; Required Fields; Frequency; Status
relationshipRule: Data Source 1:M Events

definition: Criteria used to distinguish an event type.
mandatoryAttributes: Event code; action; category; message type; SPL filter
relationshipRule: One or more identifiers per event

definition: Expected arrival interval or volume profile for an event.
mandatoryAttributes: Frequency type; interval; baseline; tolerance
relationshipRule: One expectation per event or environment

definition: Governed health-check template used to validate event availability, quality, parsing, timeliness, volume, field completeness and collection behaviour.
mandatoryAttributes: Event ID; Check Type; SPL or Method; Threshold; Schedule; Owner; Status
relationshipRule: Data Quality & Health Checks 1:M health-check templates

definition: Confirms that an event exists and arrives within an acceptable delay.
mandatoryAttributes: Window; expected count; latency threshold
relationshipRule: Optional check per event

definition: Detects unusual event counts, missing periods and duplicate records.
mandatoryAttributes: Baseline; warning threshold; critical threshold; duplicate key
relationshipRule: Optional check per event

definition: Validates event boundaries, line breaking, timestamp extraction, timezone behaviour and props.conf timestamp configuration.
mandatoryAttributes: Expected sample; parsing rules; time skew threshold
relationshipRule: Optional check per event

definition: Validates required fields, extracted fields, null rates, value formats, allowed values and normalisation quality.
mandatoryAttributes: Required fields; value constraints; null threshold
relationshipRule: Optional check per event

definition: Assessment of event and sourcetype mapping to Splunk Common Information Model or equivalent data model.
mandatoryAttributes: Data model; dataset; tags; required fields; compliance status
relationshipRule: Event or component 1:0..M CIM assessments

definition: Execution result for a component, source or event health check.
mandatoryAttributes: Check ID; entity ID; result; checked time; metric; evidence
relationshipRule: Health Check 1:M Results

definition: Defines the Splunk sourcetype identity and its relationship to vendor/product, technology mapping and data models.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; owner; status
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M sourcetype identity metadata

definition: Splunk event classification used for parsing, timestamp handling, field extraction and knowledge mapping.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; description; vendor/product; CIM/data model mapping; owner; status
relationshipRule: Sourcetype Identity 1:M sourcetype values

definition: Human-readable description of what the sourcetype represents and when it should be used.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; description
relationshipRule: Sourcetype 1:1 description

definition: Mapping from sourcetype to source vendor, product, technology family or product examples.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; vendor; product; technology
relationshipRule: Sourcetype M:M vendor/product mappings

definition: Mapping from sourcetype to Splunk CIM, ECS or another governed data model.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; data model; dataset; status
relationshipRule: Sourcetype M:M data model mappings

definition: Defines raw event format, encoding, event boundaries, line breaking and multi-line handling.
mandatoryAttributes: Data format; line breaker; event boundary rule; encoding
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M event-format metadata

definition: Raw event data format such as JSON, XML, CEF, LEEF, CSV, TSV, key-value, syslog, Windows Event XML or plain text.
mandatoryAttributes: Format name; example; parser mode
relationshipRule: Event Format 1:M data formats

definition: Character encoding or charset needed to safely parse the event stream.
mandatoryAttributes: Encoding; charset; validation status
relationshipRule: Event Format 1:M encoding rules

definition: Rule that determines where one event ends and the next event starts.
mandatoryAttributes: LINE_BREAKER; SHOULD_LINEMERGE; example event
relationshipRule: Event Format 1:M line-breaking rules

definition: Configuration and validation for events that span multiple physical lines.
mandatoryAttributes: Multiline indicator; merge rule; test sample
relationshipRule: Event Format 1:M multiline rules

definition: Props.conf, transforms.conf or equivalent parser stanza that shapes events for a sourcetype. Input stanzas remain under TAX-03.04.01.
mandatoryAttributes: Stanza name; sourcetype; app; owner; status
relationshipRule: Sourcetype 1:M parsing stanzas

definition: Known raw-event prefix, header, preamble or field label that appears before the meaningful event body or timestamp.
mandatoryAttributes: Prefix; location; extraction rule
relationshipRule: Event Format 1:M header or prefix patterns

definition: Defines timestamp discovery, format, precision, timezone and Splunk props.conf timestamp settings.
mandatoryAttributes: Datetime format; timezone; TIME_FORMAT; TIME_PREFIX
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M timestamp-handling metadata

definition: Timestamp representation found in the event, such as ISO 8601, RFC 3339, Unix epoch seconds, Unix epoch milliseconds, syslog or Windows File Time.
mandatoryAttributes: Format name; sample; Splunk TIME_FORMAT
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M datetime formats

definition: Where the authoritative event time appears in the raw event.
mandatoryAttributes: Location; field name; offset; example
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M timestamp locations

definition: Prefix or pattern immediately before the timestamp, including Splunk TIME_PREFIX guidance.
mandatoryAttributes: TIME_PREFIX; sample; confidence
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M timestamp-prefix rules

definition: Timezone or UTC offset handling for the event timestamp.
mandatoryAttributes: Timezone; offset; normalised UTC flag
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M timezone rules

definition: Granularity of the timestamp, such as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds.
mandatoryAttributes: Precision; sample; validation status
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M timestamp-precision rules

definition: Splunk TIME_FORMAT value used to parse the event timestamp.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; TIME_FORMAT; sample timestamp
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M TIME_FORMAT definitions

definition: Splunk MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD value used to limit timestamp discovery in raw events.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; lookahead; evidence
relationshipRule: Timestamp Handling 1:M timestamp-lookahead definitions

definition: Splunk SHOULD_LINEMERGE setting used when determining whether physical lines should be merged into an event.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; SHOULD_LINEMERGE; justification
relationshipRule: Timestamp and line-breaking setting linked to event structure

definition: Splunk LINE_BREAKER setting used to define event boundaries.
mandatoryAttributes: Sourcetype; LINE_BREAKER; sample event
relationshipRule: Timestamp and line-breaking setting linked to event structure

definition: Defines required fields, extracted fields, regex, aliases, calculated fields, lookups and normalisation to CIM or another data model.
mandatoryAttributes: Required fields; extraction rules; normalisation status
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M field extraction and normalisation metadata

definition: Minimum fields required for the event type or sourcetype to support detection, investigation and assurance.
mandatoryAttributes: Field name; requirement level; purpose
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M required fields

definition: Fields extracted from raw events during search time or index time.
mandatoryAttributes: Field name; extraction method; sourcetype
relationshipRule: Sourcetype/Event 1:M extracted fields

definition: Regular expression used to extract or validate fields.
mandatoryAttributes: Regex; sample; target field
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M regex rules

definition: Splunk-compatible named capture regex using field names for extraction.
mandatoryAttributes: Named regex; sample; target fields
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M Splunk named regex rules

definition: Alias mapping from vendor-specific field names to common or CIM field names.
mandatoryAttributes: Source field; alias field; app; owner
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M field aliases

definition: Derived fields created from other field values.
mandatoryAttributes: Calculated field; expression; sourcetype
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M calculated fields

definition: Lookup enrichment used to normalise, enrich or classify event fields.
mandatoryAttributes: Lookup name; key fields; output fields; owner
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M lookups

definition: Normalisation of fields and values to Splunk Common Information Model or equivalent.
mandatoryAttributes: Data model; dataset; field mapping; status
relationshipRule: Field Metadata 1:M normalisation mappings

definition: Defines expected frequency, expected volume, noise level, value level and priority for event types and sourcetypes.
mandatoryAttributes: Expected frequency; volume; noise; value; priority
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M event-behaviour metadata

definition: Expected event volume, EPS or daily ingest profile for a sourcetype or event type.
mandatoryAttributes: Expected volume; unit; baseline period
relationshipRule: Event Behaviour 1:M expected volume rules

definition: Indicative event noise level used to prioritise filtering, detection and storage decisions.
mandatoryAttributes: Noise rating; rationale; owner
relationshipRule: Event Behaviour 1:M noise ratings

definition: Indicative security value of the event type or sourcetype.
mandatoryAttributes: Value rating; rationale; use cases
relationshipRule: Event Behaviour 1:M value ratings

definition: Collection or assurance priority for the event type or sourcetype.
mandatoryAttributes: Priority; rationale; status
relationshipRule: Event Behaviour 1:M priority assignments

definition: Defines processing rules and decisions that shape events before or during ingestion, including parsing, masking, filtering, retention or suppression decisions, enrichment, transformation, source or sourcetype rewrite and timestamp rewrite rules. Ingest Processor rule logic belongs here; the Ingest Processor component and routes belong under TAX-03.
mandatoryAttributes: Parsing rule; masking rule; enrichment rule; transform rule
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M event-processing and shaping rules; may be implemented in props/transforms, Ingest Processor pipelines, ingest actions or equivalent processing tiers.

definition: Rule that parses event content into structured fields or event boundaries.
mandatoryAttributes: Rule name; sourcetype; app; test sample
relationshipRule: Event Processing 1:M parsing rules

definition: Rule used to mask, redact or protect sensitive values before storage or exposure.
mandatoryAttributes: Rule name; target field; masking method; approval
relationshipRule: Event Processing 1:M masking rules

definition: Rule used to enrich events with contextual fields or lookup data.
mandatoryAttributes: Rule name; enrichment source; output fields
relationshipRule: Event Processing 1:M enrichment rules

definition: Transforms.conf, ingest action or equivalent event transformation rule that shapes data for a sourcetype.
mandatoryAttributes: Transform name; source; target; status
relationshipRule: Event Processing 1:M transform rules

definition: Defines security use cases, required data and events, detection analytics, response actions, validation and coverage.
mandatoryAttributes: Domain name; steward; status
relationshipRule: Root domain

definition: Defines the security behaviour, threat scenario, control objective and threat mapping that establish why detection is required.
relationshipRule: Groups related detection and response entities.

definition: Defines the data sources and event types required to support a security use case.
relationshipRule: Groups related detection and response entities.

definition: Defines the searches, correlation rules, risk rules, thresholds and models that implement detection logic.
relationshipRule: Groups related detection and response entities.

definition: Defines operational response actions and the approved governance artefacts that direct investigation, escalation, containment, remediation and recovery.
mandatoryAttributes: Response action; owner; incident response plan reference; runbook reference; escalation matrix reference; shared responsibility matrix reference
relationshipRule: A response contains one or more actions and may reference approved plans, runbooks, escalation artefacts and shared-responsibility assignments maintained under TAX-02.07.
notes: Keep approved document metadata under TAX-02.07. TAX-05 records response actions and references the applicable governance artefacts and responsibility assignments.

definition: Defines testing, validation status, available telemetry, implemented analytics and remaining detection gaps.
relationshipRule: Groups related detection and response entities.

definition: Security behaviour, threat scenario or control objective requiring detection.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case Name; Platform ID; Owner; Priority; Status; Threat Mapping; Validation Status
relationshipRule: Platform 1:M Use Cases

definition: Mapping to MITRE ATT&CK tactic, technique, sub-technique or threat scenario.
mandatoryAttributes: Framework; tactic; technique; sub-technique; scenario
relationshipRule: Use Case M:M Threat Mappings

definition: Bridge recording data source requirements for a use case.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case ID; Data Source ID; Requirement Type; Coverage Status
relationshipRule: Use Cases M:M Data Sources

definition: Bridge recording event requirements for a use case.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case ID; Event ID; Mandatory or Optional; Validation Status
relationshipRule: Use Cases M:M Events

definition: Technical SPL, correlation search, risk rule, threshold or model implementing a use case.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case ID; Name; SPL; Owner; Version; Status; Schedule
relationshipRule: Use Case 1:M Detection Analytics

definition: Notable event, SOAR playbook, investigation guide and escalation action.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case ID; response type; owner; reference; status
relationshipRule: Use Case 1:M Response Actions

definition: Test scenario and result proving the use case and analytic operate as intended.
mandatoryAttributes: Use Case ID; expected events; test method; result; last validated
relationshipRule: Use Case 1:M Validation Records

definition: Assessment of available data, implemented analytics and validation status.
mandatoryAttributes: Source ID; coverage status; gaps; use cases; last assessed
relationshipRule: Platform or source 1:M coverage assessments

definition: Defines repeatable scored assessments of event-data quality. Detailed evidence and criterion results remain in TAX-04; TAX-06 consumes only derived assurance roll-ups.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment ID; assessed entity; assessment type; score; rating; assessment date; method; assessor; evidence
relationshipRule: A data source, sourcetype or event type may have multiple dated assessments and one current approved assessment per assessment type.
sourceWorksheet: Timestamp Quality Calculator / Data Quality Assessments
notes: Scores should be reproducible from retained evidence. Do not duplicate detailed assessment evidence in TAX-06.

definition: Assesses whether event timestamps are consistent, explicit, precise, complete, representative of occurrence time and deterministically parseable by Splunk.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessed data source or sourcetype; six criterion scores; total score; rating; assessment date; method; evidence
relationshipRule: A data source or sourcetype may have multiple timestamp assessments over time; the latest approved result may feed the data-source assurance roll-up.
notes: Calculator total is 0-24 across six criteria scored 0-4.

definition: Numeric total produced from the six timestamp-quality criteria.
mandatoryAttributes: Score from 0 to 24; criteria completed
relationshipRule: One total score per timestamp assessment, calculated as the sum of six criterion scores.
notes: Do not compare scores unless the same criteria and scoring version were used.

definition: Controlled rating derived from the timestamp quality score.
mandatoryAttributes: Exceptional 22-24; Good 18-21; Fair 13-17; Poor 7-12; Fail 0-6
relationshipRule: Exactly one rating is derived for each completed timestamp assessment.
notes: Exceptional is production-ready and highly reliable; Fail requires correction, transformation or enrichment before ingestion.

definition: Stores the six individual 0-4 criterion results used to calculate timestamp quality.
mandatoryAttributes: Format Consistency; Timezone Quality; Timestamp Precision; Completeness and Ambiguity; Event-Time Reliability; Splunk Parsing Complexity
relationshipRule: Each completed timestamp assessment has exactly six criterion results.
notes: Event-Time Reliability considers source clock synchronisation, buffering and forwarding delay, not only visible timestamp format.

definition: Date and time when the timestamp assessment was performed or approved.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment date; effective date; assessor
relationshipRule: One assessment date per assessment record.
notes: Reassess after source, parsing, timezone or transport changes.

definition: Identifies the calculator, test procedure, sample scope and scoring version used.
mandatoryAttributes: Method name; scoring version; sample period; sample size
relationshipRule: One documented method per assessment.
notes: Recommended method: Splunk Timestamp Quality Calculator with retained sample evidence.

definition: References samples, SPL results, parsing configuration and notes supporting each criterion score.
mandatoryAttributes: Evidence reference; sample; SPL or configuration reference; notes; owner
relationshipRule: A timestamp assessment may reference one or more evidence records.
notes: Avoid storing secrets or sensitive raw events directly in the taxonomy.

definition: Measures whether required and expected fields are populated across the assessed event population.
mandatoryAttributes: Required fields; population; completeness score; exceptions; evidence
relationshipRule: One or more dated completeness assessments per data source, sourcetype or event type.

definition: Assesses the inherent quality, consistency and machine-parseability of the source log format using repeatable criteria covering structure, delimitation, schema, event boundaries, encoding, integrity and Splunk parsing complexity.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessed data source or sourcetype; source log format; six criterion scores; total score; rating; assessment date; method; evidence; remediation requirement
relationshipRule: A data source or sourcetype may have multiple log-format quality assessments over time; each assessment should identify the sample, scoring version and evidence used.
notes: Calculator total is 0-24 across six criteria scored 0-4. This broader assessment replaces the former Parsing Quality Assessment; parsing complexity is retained as one criterion.

definition: Numeric score produced by the log-format quality assessment.
mandatoryAttributes: Score from 0 to 24; criteria completed
relationshipRule: A score is valid only when all required criteria use the same scoring version.
notes: Record the unweighted total unless a governed weighting method is explicitly defined.

definition: Qualitative rating derived from the log-format quality score.
mandatoryAttributes: Exceptional 22-24; Good 18-21; Fair 13-17; Poor 7-12; Fail 0-6
relationshipRule: The rating must be derived from the recorded score using the approved threshold set.
notes: Exceptional indicates a highly consistent and readily parseable format; Fail indicates substantial correction, transformation or custom engineering is required.

definition: Assesses whether events follow a stable, predictable and documented structure across the representative sample.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; observed structures; variance; exceptions; evidence
relationshipRule: Structural consistency should be assessed across representative event types and operating conditions.
notes: Examples include stable JSON objects, consistent CEF headers, or documented positional records.

definition: Assesses whether fields, delimiters, quoting and escaped characters can be separated reliably without ambiguity.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; delimiter; quoting rule; escape rule; embedded delimiter behaviour; evidence
relationshipRule: The assessment should test embedded delimiters, quotes, line breaks and special characters.
notes: Relevant to CSV, TSV, key-value, CEF, LEEF and other delimited formats.

definition: Assesses whether fields have explicit names, stable keys or dependable positional definitions supported by a schema or specification.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; schema availability; field names; version; undocumented fields; evidence
relationshipRule: Schema quality should identify versioning and behaviour when fields are added, removed or reordered.
notes: Named JSON fields generally score higher than undocumented positional fields.

definition: Assesses whether individual events can be separated deterministically without accidental merging or splitting.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; boundary method; multiline behaviour; line breaker; truncation risk; evidence
relationshipRule: Event-boundary assessment should include multiline payloads, stack traces, embedded newlines and transport framing where relevant.
notes: Link to TAX-04 parsing and line-breaking configuration when Splunk settings are required.

definition: Assesses character encoding, payload completeness, corruption, truncation and preservation of source values during collection and transport.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; encoding; invalid characters; truncation; corruption; completeness; evidence
relationshipRule: Assessment should distinguish source defects from collector, transport or Splunk ingestion defects.
notes: Examples include UTF-8 validity, byte-order marks, binary contamination and maximum-event-size truncation.

definition: Assesses the level of Splunk configuration, preprocessing, transformation or custom engineering required to parse the format reliably.
mandatoryAttributes: Criterion score 0-4; required configuration; custom transforms; preprocessing; maintainability; evidence
relationshipRule: Higher quality scores represent lower parsing complexity and greater use of deterministic native parsing.
notes: Reference props.conf, transforms.conf, ingest actions, Edge Processor or Ingest Processor configuration where applicable.

definition: Records when the log-format quality assessment was performed and when its result became effective.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment date; effective date; assessor; next review date
relationshipRule: Reassess after source-version, schema, transport, parser or collection-path changes.

definition: Records the calculator, scoring version, sample scope and procedure used to produce the assessment.
mandatoryAttributes: Method name; scoring version; sample period; sample size; event types sampled
relationshipRule: Assessment results should be reproducible using the retained method and evidence.
notes: Recommended method: Splunk Log Format Quality Calculator.

definition: References representative raw events, schemas, test results, SPL, parser configuration and other evidence supporting the score.
mandatoryAttributes: Evidence reference; sample reference; schema; SPL or configuration reference; owner; retention location
relationshipRule: Evidence should be sufficient to reproduce each criterion score without storing secrets or unnecessarily sensitive raw data.

definition: Records corrective actions required when the format does not meet the approved quality threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Finding; affected criterion; remediation action; owner; due date; status; acceptance decision
relationshipRule: Each failing or materially weak criterion should link to remediation, accepted risk or an approved compensating control.
notes: Examples: source format change, parser correction, line-breaking fix, encoding conversion, truncation remediation or preprocessing.

definition: Measures consistency of formats, field names, values, schemas and event structures over time and across producers.
mandatoryAttributes: Consistency dimensions; score; variance; exceptions; evidence
relationshipRule: One or more dated consistency assessments per governed data population.

definition: Measures duplicate-event rates and the reliability of unique event or transaction identifiers.
mandatoryAttributes: Duplicate rate; identifier fields; replay tolerance; evidence
relationshipRule: One or more dated uniqueness assessments per data source or sourcetype.

definition: Measures ingestion latency, event delay, collection lag and compliance with timeliness objectives.
mandatoryAttributes: Latency metric; objective; percentile; breach rate; evidence
relationshipRule: One or more dated timeliness assessments per data source or sourcetype.
notes: Timestamp quality and event timeliness are related but distinct: a correct event timestamp can still arrive late.

definition: Measures mapping completeness and conformance to required Splunk Common Information Model datasets and fields.
mandatoryAttributes: CIM data model; required fields; mapping result; score; evidence
relationshipRule: One or more dated CIM assessments per sourcetype or event type.

definition: Derived overall score or rating combining approved data-quality assessment dimensions.
mandatoryAttributes: Timestamp quality assessment reference; log format quality assessment reference; other component assessment references; weighting version; total score; rating; calculation date
relationshipRule: At most one current approved overall data-quality result per governed entity and scoring version.
notes: The calculation must retain links to timestamp, log-format and other component assessments and must not conceal a failing critical dimension.

definition: Defines onboarding and viability, dependency relationships, assurance roll-ups, and lifecycle state and review information.
mandatoryAttributes: Domain name; steward; status
relationshipRule: Root domain

definition: Groups onboarding lifecycle records and pre-onboarding viability assessments used to decide whether a source should proceed to detailed design and implementation.
mandatoryAttributes: Onboarding record; viability assessment; decision; phase; next action
relationshipRule: A platform or data source may have one or more onboarding and viability records across its lifecycle.
notes: Viability is assessed before detailed design; onboarding records track accepted work through implementation and operation.

definition: Defines technical, operational, platform and data dependencies that affect collection, processing, detection, assurance or service continuity.
mandatoryAttributes: Upstream entity; downstream entity; dependency type; criticality; owner; failure impact
relationshipRule: Any governed entity may have zero or more upstream and downstream dependencies.
notes: Use dependency records to support lineage, impact analysis and resilience planning.

definition: Groups derived platform and data-source assurance roll-ups that summarise governance, collection, event quality, CIM and detection coverage status.
mandatoryAttributes: Entity ID; component health; event health; governance status; coverage status; overall result
relationshipRule: Each governed platform or data source may have one current assurance roll-up derived from its underlying evidence.
notes: Roll-ups are derived views and should not duplicate source health, governance or detection records.

definition: Defines controlled lifecycle states and the review, expiry and renewal information used across governed taxonomy entities.
mandatoryAttributes: Current state; effective date; last review; next review; expiry; reviewer; outcome
relationshipRule: A governed entity has one current lifecycle state and may have multiple historical review records.
notes: Use consistently across platforms, sources, components, governance artefacts and analytics.

definition: Tracks onboarding progress, approvals, readiness and go-live.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; Data Source ID; Event ID; owner; phase; status; due date
relationshipRule: Platform or source 1:M onboarding records

definition: Directed relationship between platforms, components, sources, events, analytics or governance artifacts.
mandatoryAttributes: Source ID; Depends On ID; relationship type; criticality; owner
relationshipRule: Entity M:M Entity

definition: Aggregated governance, source, component and event assurance status for a platform.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; governance status; source health; component health; event health; overall status
relationshipRule: One current roll-up per platform

definition: Aggregated health, quality and coverage status for a data source, derived from current approved evidence including TAX-04.09 data-quality assessments.
mandatoryAttributes: Data Source ID; input health; event health; timestamp quality score and rating; log format quality score and rating; overall data quality score; CIM status; coverage status
relationshipRule: One current roll-up per data source; detailed scores and evidence remain in TAX-04.09 and are referenced rather than duplicated.
sourceWorksheet: Data Sources / Event Health Checks / Data Quality Assessments
notes: Timestamp, log-format and overall data-quality values must identify the source assessment, scoring version and assessment date. Detailed evidence remains under TAX-04.09.

definition: Controlled state used consistently across entities.
mandatoryAttributes: Planned; Onboarding; Active; Degraded; Retired; Expired; Exception
relationshipRule: One current state per entity

definition: Dates and outcomes that drive periodic review or expiry.
mandatoryAttributes: Last review; next review; expiry; reviewer; outcome
relationshipRule: Zero or more review records

definition: Defines a Splunk Ingest Processor instance used to receive, process and route data before indexing or external storage.
relationshipRule: Input Component may be an Ingest Processor when collection requires managed pipeline processing before final routing.
notes: Component placement only. Pipeline rules that alter events are governed under TAX-04.08.

definition: Defines the Splunk Deployment Server relationship used to distribute and manage applications and configuration that implement or support event collection on deployment clients.
mandatoryAttributes: Deployment Server reference; managed deployment client or client group; server class; deployment app; collection purpose; configuration type; owner; status
relationshipRule: A collection input may be managed by one Deployment Server through one or more server classes and deployment apps. A server class may target multiple deployment clients and distribute multiple deployment apps.
notes: The Deployment Server platform identity remains under TAX-01.05.01. This branch governs the collection-specific configuration and assignment relationships.

definition: Identifies the managed Deployment Server platform responsible for distributing the collection configuration.
mandatoryAttributes: Deployment Server ID; platform ID; hostname; environment; status
relationshipRule: References one TAX-01.05.01 Deployment Server platform record.
notes: Reference only; platform ownership and lifecycle remain under TAX-01.

definition: Defines a Universal Forwarder, Heavy Forwarder or other supported deployment client that receives collection configuration from a Deployment Server.
mandatoryAttributes: Client name; client GUID; client type; operating system; environment; Deployment Server; last phone-home; status
relationshipRule: A deployment client is managed by one Deployment Server at a time and may match one or more server classes.
notes: Link the client to the collector or input component it hosts where applicable.

definition: Defines the Deployment Server targeting rule used to group deployment clients and assign collection applications or configuration.
mandatoryAttributes: Server class name; description; include rules; exclude rules; machine filters; restart behaviour; owner; status
relationshipRule: A server class may target many deployment clients and may be assigned many deployment apps.
notes: Use for intended targeting logic. Actual matched-client membership is recorded separately.

definition: Defines the deployable application package containing event-collection or supporting configuration distributed by the Deployment Server.
mandatoryAttributes: Deployment app name; version; purpose; configuration files; input type; target sourcetype; target index; restart requirement; owner; status
relationshipRule: A deployment app may be assigned to many server classes and may contain one or more collection configurations.
sourceWorksheet: Taxonomy Register / Apps & TAs / Manual Addition
notes: Typical files include inputs.conf, outputs.conf, props.conf, transforms.conf and scripted or modular input configuration. Link reusable app or TA identity to TAX-03.03.03 where applicable.

definition: Defines which deployment apps are assigned to a server class and therefore intended for distribution to matching deployment clients.
mandatoryAttributes: Deployment Server; server class; deployment app; assignment purpose; effective date; owner; status
relationshipRule: Server Class M:M Deployment App through an assignment record.
notes: Use to distinguish intended app assignment from actual client receipt or deployment state.

definition: Defines the deployment clients that currently match or are assigned to a server class.
mandatoryAttributes: Deployment Server; deployment client; server class; match basis; last evaluated; status
relationshipRule: Deployment Client M:M Server Class through a membership record.
notes: Supports assurance checks comparing intended targeting rules with actual matched clients.

definition: Named pipeline that receives one or more source streams and applies ordered routing and processing stages before delivery.
relationshipRule: Ingest Processor 1:M pipelines; a pipeline may contain routing decisions and references to event-processing rules governed under TAX-04.08.
notes: Use for pipeline identity, ownership, source mapping and high-level delivery path.

definition: Route inside an Ingest Processor pipeline that determines which events are delivered to which destination or processing branch.
relationshipRule: Ingest Processor Pipeline 1:M routes; route conditions may reference source, sourcetype, metadata, event fields or processing outcomes.
notes: Use for routing flow. Use TAX-04.08 for the event-transforming rule content.

definition: Rule that maps a pipeline or route to the final delivery destination such as Splunk index, Splunk Cloud destination, S3, federated storage or another approved target.
relationshipRule: Pipeline or route 1:M destination rules; destination rules connect ingest processing to approved storage and index destinations.
notes: Keep index, storage and delivery selection here rather than under sourcetype parsing.

definition: Routing decision that keeps, drops or redirects events based on approved collection policy before final destination selection.
relationshipRule: Pipeline or route 1:M drop/keep routing decisions; where the rule changes event structure, link to TAX-04.08.
notes: Use this for routing intent. Use TAX-04.08.06 when the condition is an event filtering rule that is part of event shaping.

definition: Defines the implemented end-to-end path through which events move from the source system to the final Splunk destination, including every collection, forwarding, processing and routing hop.
mandatoryAttributes: Topology ID; topology name; source node; collection path; destination node; logging pattern reference; status
relationshipRule: Each data-source input mapping must reference one implemented collection topology. A topology must reference an approved logging pattern and may contain one or more ordered nodes and connections. Any deviation from the approved pattern must be documented.
notes: The logging pattern is the reusable reference architecture; the collection topology records the actual deployed path for a specific onboarding.

definition: Classifies whether a proposed or implemented collection path is approved, recommended, supported, conditionally supported, legacy, lab-only, deprecated or prohibited.
mandatoryAttributes: Collection topology or pattern reference; support status; supporting authority; conditions; rationale; review date
relationshipRule: Each implemented collection topology should have one current support status and may retain historical status records for audit purposes.
notes: Recommended values: Recommended; Supported; Conditionally Supported; Legacy; Lab / Proof of Concept Only; Deprecated; Prohibited.

definition: Unique identifier for an implemented collection topology.
mandatoryAttributes: Topology ID
relationshipRule: One identifier per implemented collection topology.
notes: Example: TOP-001.

definition: Human-readable name and purpose of the implemented collection topology.
mandatoryAttributes: Topology name; purpose; environment
relationshipRule: One descriptive record per topology.
notes: Example: FortiGate Production Syslog Collection.

definition: Identifies the system, application, appliance or service that originates the events represented by the topology.
mandatoryAttributes: Source system reference; source role; environment
relationshipRule: Each topology must contain at least one source node linked to the relevant TAX-01 system and TAX-03 data source.
notes: Example: FortiGate firewall cluster.

definition: Defines an ordered intermediary component through which events pass, such as a syslog server, Universal Forwarder, Heavy Forwarder, Azure Function, Event Hub, SC4S or Ingest Processor.
mandatoryAttributes: Sequence; component reference; component role; hosting context; status
relationshipRule: A topology may contain zero or more ordered collection hops. Each hop should reference the relevant collection component under TAX-03.03.
notes: Repeat this node for each intermediary component in path order.

definition: Identifies the final Splunk receiving or storage destination for the event stream.
mandatoryAttributes: Destination platform; receiving endpoint; destination index or storage tier
relationshipRule: Each topology must contain at least one final destination node linked to the applicable Splunk platform and index destination.
notes: Examples: Splunk Cloud HEC; Splunk Enterprise indexer cluster; S3 archive destination.

definition: Defines the directed connection between two adjacent topology nodes, including protocol, port, security zone and delivery behaviour.
mandatoryAttributes: From node; to node; sequence; transport reference; port; security zone; encryption
relationshipRule: Each adjacent pair of nodes in the implemented path must have a directed connection. Transport details should reference TAX-03.02.02.
notes: Example: FortiGate → Syslog Server using TCP 514 across the network-security zone.

definition: Provides the ordered, human-readable representation of the complete implemented event path.
mandatoryAttributes: Ordered path
relationshipRule: Derived from the ordered source, hop, destination and connection records.
notes: Example: FortiGate → Syslog Server → Universal Forwarder → Splunk Enterprise Indexer Cluster.

definition: Records whether the implemented topology conforms to its approved logging pattern and identifies any approved deviations.
mandatoryAttributes: Logging pattern ID; conformance status; deviation; approval reference
relationshipRule: Each topology must reference one approved logging pattern. Non-conforming implementations require a documented deviation and approval.
notes: Suggested values: Conforms; Conforms with approved deviation; Does not conform; Not assessed.

definition: References the diagram, architecture document or machine-readable graph representing the implemented collection topology.
mandatoryAttributes: Document or diagram reference; version; owner
relationshipRule: A topology may reference one or more current diagrams or architecture artefacts.
notes: May contain a document ID, URL, repository path, Mermaid definition, draw.io file or Visio reference.

definition: Governed rule within an Ingest Processor pipeline that evaluates, transforms, enriches, filters, masks, rewrites or otherwise shapes event data.
relationshipRule: Ingest Processor Pipeline 1:M rules; rules may reference event format, timestamp handling, field extraction, event behaviour or routing metadata.
notes: Rule logic belongs here; pipeline and route placement belongs under TAX-03.02.03.

definition: Rule that includes, excludes, samples or suppresses events based on raw content, metadata, fields, sourcetype, source, host, index or detection value.
relationshipRule: Processing rule may filter events before storage; routing effect should be linked to TAX-03.02.03 when it affects destination selection.
notes: Use with clear collection approval because filtering can create blind spots.

definition: Rule that changes raw event structure, field names, field values, metadata, nesting, format or payload shape before indexing or storage.
relationshipRule: Processing rule 1:M transformations; may be implemented as Ingest Processor processing, ingest actions, transforms.conf or equivalent.
notes: Use for normalising or restructuring events; keep destination routing under TAX-03.02.03.

definition: Rule that masks, redacts, hashes or removes sensitive field values before storage, exposure or downstream processing.
relationshipRule: Processing rule may protect sensitive data; should link to approval, data classification and validation evidence.
notes: Useful for secrets, tokens, personal data and sensitive payload elements.

definition: Rule that rewrites source, sourcetype, host or other Splunk metadata to align events with governed sourcetype identity and routing expectations.
relationshipRule: Processing rule may update metadata; sourcetype identity remains governed by TAX-04.01 and routing by TAX-03.02.03.
notes: Use when Ingest Processor or equivalent logic changes metadata before indexing.

definition: Rule that rewrites, normalises or derives event timestamp values before storage, usually to fix inconsistent time formats, missing timezone offsets or incorrect event-time fields.
relationshipRule: Processing rule may reference timestamp handling definitions under TAX-04.03 and validation checks under TAX-04 data quality.
notes: Use with validation evidence to ensure event time is preserved correctly.

definition: Records the approved decision to retain, suppress, sample, aggregate or filter events before they are indexed, including where the decision is implemented and the security or operational rationale.
mandatoryAttributes: Data source; event category or condition; decision; implementation tier; rationale; risk owner; approval; review date; validation evidence
relationshipRule: A data source may have multiple pre-ingest filtering decisions. Each decision should reference the affected event categories and the source-side, collector, Ingest Processor, Heavy Forwarder or other enforcement point.
owner: Data Engineering / Security Operations / Risk Owner
notes: Distinguish source-side suppression from downstream filtering. Record events disabled at source, dropped by SC4S or Ingest Processor, sampled, aggregated or retained in full. Security-relevant exclusions require explicit approval.

definition: Defines the event types contained within a sourcetype or data source, including identifiers, expected frequency and CIM mapping.
mandatoryAttributes: Event name; identifier; expected frequency; CIM mapping; status
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M event type definitions

definition: Defines data-quality and health-check controls for sourcetypes, events, timestamps, parsing, field quality, volume, timeliness and assurance results.
mandatoryAttributes: Check type; pass criteria; failure action; evidence; owner
relationshipRule: TAX-04 1:M data-quality and health-check definitions

definition: Defines how Splunk collectors, functions, scripts, APIs, forwarders and HEC integrations authenticate for log collection.
mandatoryAttributes: Authentication method; credential type; owner; permission scope; secret storage; rotation; validation state
relationshipRule: TAX-03 1:M data-collection authentication requirements; applies to add-ons, collectors, forwarders, scripts, functions, API clients, cloud roles and HEC/token based inputs.
notes: This is for the logging integration authentication path. Use TAX-01.03.07 for the source system or application authentication model.

definition: The method used by the logging integration to authenticate, such as API token, OAuth2, client credentials, basic authentication, certificate, managed identity, IAM role, HEC token or mutual TLS.
mandatoryAttributes: Method name; protocol; applicable collection pattern; status
relationshipRule: Data collection authentication 1:M methods; each collection pattern should identify the approved authentication method.
notes: Examples: API key, bearer token, OAuth2 client credentials, Entra app registration, IAM role, certificate, HEC token, mTLS.

definition: The credential material used by the collection integration, such as password, bearer token, API key, client secret, private key, certificate, SAS key, access key or HEC token.
mandatoryAttributes: Credential type; sensitivity; storage location; rotation requirement
relationshipRule: Collection authentication method 1:M credential types; credential material must have an approved storage and rotation model.
notes: Do not store secret values in the taxonomy. Record metadata only.

definition: The team or accountable owner responsible for creating, approving, rotating, disabling and validating the collection credential or integration identity.
mandatoryAttributes: Owner team; technical contact; approval owner; escalation path
relationshipRule: Credential 1:1 owning team; collection onboarding should not proceed without an identified credential owner.
notes: Useful for operational handover and expired-token incident response.

definition: Named service account, application identity, integration account or workload identity used by the collection mechanism.
mandatoryAttributes: Account name; account type; owner; enabled state; MFA/conditional-access exception if applicable
relationshipRule: Collection integration may use one or more service accounts or workload identities; each identity should have a defined owner and permission scope.
notes: Examples: svc-splunk-azure-logs, Entra app registration, AWS IAM role, GCP service account.

definition: API key, bearer token, HEC token, personal access token or vendor token used by the collection integration to access or send log data.
mandatoryAttributes: Token type; owner; scope; expiry; rotation requirement; storage location
relationshipRule: Token-based collection authentication must link to credential storage, rotation, expiry and permission-scope validation.
notes: Use metadata only. Never store the token value in the taxonomy.

definition: OAuth flow, client ID, client credential and token endpoint configuration used by a collection integration to authenticate to an API or cloud service.
mandatoryAttributes: Tenant/authority; client ID; flow type; scopes; token endpoint; secret/certificate reference
relationshipRule: OAuth collection authentication should map scopes to the minimum log-read permissions required for the integration.
notes: Examples: Entra app registration client credentials, vendor OAuth application, SOAR/API OAuth client.

definition: Certificate, private key, mutual TLS or signed identity material used for collection authentication or trusted transport.
mandatoryAttributes: Certificate subject; issuer; expiry; key owner; storage location; renewal process
relationshipRule: Certificate-based collection authentication should include expiry, owner and renewal validation to prevent collection outages.
notes: Can apply to mTLS syslog, forwarder trust, API client certificate and cloud app registrations.

definition: Cloud-managed workload identity used by a function, collector, pipeline or hosted component to authenticate without stored secrets.
mandatoryAttributes: Identity name; cloud provider; resource binding; permission scope; owner
relationshipRule: Workload identity should be bound to the collection component and scoped to the minimum log-read or log-send permissions required.
notes: Examples: Azure Managed Identity, AWS IAM Role for Service Account, GCP Workload Identity Federation.

definition: Cloud role, policy, permission assignment or cross-account trust used by the collection integration to access cloud logs, queues, buckets, APIs or event streams.
mandatoryAttributes: Role/policy name; resource scope; actions; trust relationship; owner; review date
relationshipRule: Cloud collection permission should link to the source data location, collection component and least-privilege validation evidence.
notes: Examples: AWS cross-account role for S3/SQS, Azure RBAC for Event Hub, GCP IAM role for Pub/Sub or Cloud Logging.

definition: Approved storage location for collection credentials or secret references, such as Splunk password store, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault or a managed secret reference.
mandatoryAttributes: Storage platform; secret reference; owner; access policy; rotation support
relationshipRule: Credential metadata should identify where the secret is stored and who can retrieve or rotate it; secret values must not be stored in the taxonomy.
notes: Use a reference name or vault path only; never include actual secret material.

definition: Rotation policy, cadence, expiry date, renewal process and validation evidence for collection credentials and certificates.
mandatoryAttributes: Rotation frequency; expiry date; owner; renewal runbook; last rotation; next rotation
relationshipRule: Credential 1:M rotation events; collection assurance should validate that expiring credentials do not create logging outages.
notes: Especially useful for OAuth secrets, certificates, HEC tokens, API tokens and SAS keys.

definition: The approved resources, actions, API scopes, queues, buckets, topics, event streams or endpoints the collection identity is allowed to access.
mandatoryAttributes: Resource scope; allowed actions; denied actions; business justification; review date
relationshipRule: Collection identity 1:M permission scopes; each scope should map to required logs and collection pattern.
notes: Examples: read audit logs only, consume Event Hub, read S3 bucket, receive from SQS, write to HEC endpoint.

definition: Evidence that the collection identity has sufficient permissions for required logs but does not have excessive administrative, write, delete or unrelated access.
mandatoryAttributes: Validation date; reviewer; test result; excessive permission findings; remediation status
relationshipRule: Permission scope should be periodically validated for least privilege and linked to onboarding or assurance evidence.
notes: Useful for audit readiness and preventing collection credentials becoming privileged backdoors.

definition: Expected failure modes, alerting, retry behaviour and operational response for authentication failures in the data collection path.
mandatoryAttributes: Failure mode; detection method; retry/backoff; alert target; runbook; owner
relationshipRule: Collection authentication should define how failures such as 401, 403, expired token, disabled account or certificate expiry are detected and remediated.
notes: Examples: 401/403 API responses, token expired, certificate expired, service account disabled, cloud role trust broken, HEC token disabled.

definition: Defines the accountable ownership roles for the platform, system, application and associated security risk.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform Owner; Technical Owner; Security Owner; Risk Owner
relationshipRule: A platform or system has named accountable ownership roles; one person or team may fulfil more than one role.
notes: Renumbered into a direct TAX-01 ownership group.

definition: Defines management-plane platforms and services used to administer, configure, deploy or monitor a platform.
mandatoryAttributes: Component type; component name; platform relationship; owner; status
relationshipRule: A platform may have zero or more management components. Configuration objects that directly govern event collection are referenced under TAX-03.
notes: Contains the managed platform identity for services such as Splunk Deployment Server. Server classes, deployment apps and deployment-client collection assignments are governed under TAX-03.03.05.

definition: Defines approved operational security plans, runbooks, procedures, escalation information, recovery documentation and responsibility artefacts used to prepare for, operate and respond to security incidents.
mandatoryAttributes: Document type; title; owner; version; approval status; effective date; review date; repository reference; scope
relationshipRule: A system, platform, service or detection response may reference one or more approved operational security documents.
notes: Stores document metadata and references rather than full document contents. Detection, collection, response and assurance objects should reference the applicable approved artefacts.

definition: The approved plan defining organisational preparation, roles, coordination, escalation, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident activities for cyber security incidents.
mandatoryAttributes: Plan title; owner; version; approval authority; effective date; review date; repository reference; scope
relationshipRule: An organisation, platform or system may reference one or more incident response plans according to scope and incident type.
notes: Examples include an enterprise cyber incident response plan and a system-specific incident response annex.

definition: Operational instructions used by analysts and engineers to investigate, contain, remediate or recover from a defined security scenario.
mandatoryAttributes: Runbook title; scenario; owner; version; status; repository reference; last test date
relationshipRule: A plan or response action may reference multiple runbooks, and a runbook may support multiple detections or systems.
notes: Examples: compromised administrator account, firewall compromise, web application compromise and collector outage.

definition: Approved repeatable procedure for routine security, platform or logging operations.
mandatoryAttributes: Procedure title; owner; version; status; repository reference; review date
relationshipRule: A system or operational task may reference one or more standard operating procedures.
notes: Examples include credential rotation, collector restart, evidence preservation and emergency configuration change procedures.

definition: Defines escalation paths, decision authorities, severity thresholds and notification responsibilities for security incidents and operational failures.
mandatoryAttributes: Title; owner; severity levels; escalation roles; contact reference; approval status; review date
relationshipRule: Incident response plans, runbooks and response actions should reference the applicable escalation matrix.
notes: Keep individual contact details in an approved controlled contact register where appropriate.

definition: Controlled reference for internal and external contacts required during incident response, recovery and escalation.
mandatoryAttributes: Register title; owner; repository reference; access classification; review date
relationshipRule: Operational plans and escalation matrices may reference one or more controlled contact registers.
notes: The taxonomy should store only metadata and a protected repository reference, not sensitive personal contact details.

definition: Approved plan for sustaining critical business services during and after a disruptive event.
mandatoryAttributes: Plan title; scope; owner; version; approval status; recovery objectives; review date; repository reference
relationshipRule: A critical system or service may reference one or more business continuity plans.
notes: Link to system criticality, business service and dependency records where available.

definition: Approved technical recovery plan for restoring systems, platforms, data and dependencies after major disruption.
mandatoryAttributes: Plan title; scope; owner; version; recovery objectives; test date; review date; repository reference
relationshipRule: A system or platform may reference one or more disaster recovery plans and associated test evidence.
notes: Link to platform dependencies, backup arrangements and recovery-test evidence where applicable.

definition: Detailed operational procedure for restoring a service, system, data source, collector or security capability after an incident or outage.
mandatoryAttributes: Procedure title; owner; scope; version; prerequisites; validation steps; repository reference
relationshipRule: A disaster recovery plan, incident runbook or affected component may reference one or more recovery procedures.
notes: Examples: restore Splunk forwarder configuration, re-establish HEC collection and recover a syslog relay.

definition: Reference from a response process, analytic or use case to the approved incident response plan that governs execution and escalation.
mandatoryAttributes: Incident response plan ID; applicability; response owner; review date
relationshipRule: A response may reference one or more approved incident response plans under TAX-02.07.01.
notes: Reference TAX-02.07.01; do not duplicate the plan content in TAX-05.

definition: Reference from a detection, use case or response action to the operational runbook used for investigation, containment, remediation or recovery.
mandatoryAttributes: Runbook ID; applicable scenario; response owner; validation status; last test date
relationshipRule: A response may reference one or more runbooks under TAX-02.07.02.
notes: Reference TAX-02.07.02 and retain execution-specific actions under TAX-05.04.01.

definition: Reference to the approved escalation matrix governing severity, notification and decision-authority requirements for the response.
mandatoryAttributes: Escalation matrix ID; applicable severity; escalation owner; review date
relationshipRule: A response may reference the applicable escalation matrix under TAX-02.07.04.
notes: Reference TAX-02.07.04.

definition: Defines how security, operational, logging, monitoring, incident response, recovery and compliance responsibilities are divided between the customer, platform owner, service provider, cloud provider, SOC and other relevant parties.
mandatoryAttributes: Matrix name; scope; applicable system or service; parties; responsibility model; owner; approval status; effective date; review date; document reference
relationshipRule: A system, platform, service, collection topology, response process or assurance record may reference one or more shared responsibility matrices according to scope.
notes: Supports RACI, RASCI, customer/vendor/cloud-provider split and other approved responsibility models. Store matrix metadata and references rather than the complete matrix where it is maintained externally.

definition: The approved title and version identifier of the shared responsibility matrix.
mandatoryAttributes: Matrix name; version
relationshipRule: Each shared responsibility matrix has one governed name and version.

definition: Defines the systems, services, environments, activities, incident types or responsibility boundaries covered by the matrix.
mandatoryAttributes: Scope description; applicable system or service; exclusions
relationshipRule: A matrix scope may cover one or more systems, services, environments or operational processes.

definition: Identifies the organisations, teams, service providers and operational roles included in the matrix.
mandatoryAttributes: Party name; party type; role; contact or owner reference
relationshipRule: A shared responsibility matrix contains two or more participating parties.
notes: Examples include customer, SaaS vendor, cloud provider, managed service provider, platform team and SOC.

definition: The model used to classify responsibility and accountability assignments.
mandatoryAttributes: Model name; role codes; model definition
relationshipRule: Each matrix uses one approved responsibility model, such as RACI, RASCI or a shared-responsibility split.
notes: Supported examples: RACI, RASCI, customer/vendor/cloud-provider split, custom approved model.

definition: Assigns a responsibility code or accountability role to a party for a defined activity, control, service, incident task or operational outcome.
mandatoryAttributes: Activity or control; party; responsibility code; accountable owner; notes
relationshipRule: Activities M:M Parties through responsibility assignments; each activity should have an accountable party where the selected model requires one.
notes: Can be referenced by TAX-03 collection ownership, TAX-05 response actions and TAX-06 assurance/remediation ownership.

definition: Records whether the shared responsibility matrix is draft, reviewed, approved, superseded or retired.
mandatoryAttributes: Status; approval authority; approval date
relationshipRule: Each matrix has one current approval status.

definition: Identifies the person, team or governance authority accountable for maintaining and reviewing the matrix.
mandatoryAttributes: Owner; deputy or support owner; contact reference
relationshipRule: Each matrix has one accountable owner and may have supporting maintainers.

definition: Records when the matrix becomes effective and when it must next be reviewed.
mandatoryAttributes: Effective date; review date; review frequency
relationshipRule: Each approved matrix has an effective date and a planned review date.

definition: Provides the repository, document identifier, URL or controlled reference used to locate the approved shared responsibility matrix.
mandatoryAttributes: Repository; document ID or URL; access classification
relationshipRule: A matrix has one or more controlled document references.
notes: Do not store secrets or uncontrolled local file paths.

definition: Records an approved deviation, unresolved ownership gap or exception to the standard responsibility allocation.
mandatoryAttributes: Exception description; affected activity; owner; risk; approval; expiry or review date
relationshipRule: A matrix may contain zero or more approved responsibility exceptions.
notes: Unassigned or disputed responsibilities should be treated as governance risks until resolved.

definition: References the approved shared responsibility matrix and assignments that define who performs, supports, approves, is consulted on and is informed about response activities.
mandatoryAttributes: Shared responsibility matrix ID; applicable scope; response activity; accountable party; review date
relationshipRule: A response may reference one or more responsibility assignments maintained under TAX-02.07.09.
notes: Reference TAX-02.07.09 and avoid duplicating the complete matrix in TAX-05.

definition: References responsibility assignments governing assurance review, control remediation, risk treatment and closure of identified data-source or platform gaps.
mandatoryAttributes: Shared responsibility matrix ID; activity; accountable party; responsible party; due date or review date
relationshipRule: An assurance or remediation record may reference one or more assignments maintained under TAX-02.07.09.
notes: Use for ownership references only; maintain the approved matrix under TAX-02.07.09.

definition: Assesses whether a candidate or existing log source provides sufficient incremental cyber-security value relative to overlap, investigative usefulness, entity coverage and ingestion volume.
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment identity; gate result; novelty; pivot density; semantic value; pivot breadth; entity coverage; value score; volume; decision; evidence; review date
relationshipRule: A candidate log source may have multiple assessments over time; one approved current result may govern the ingestion decision.
notes: Complements onboarding viability: viability asks whether the source can be onboarded; this assessment asks whether it is worth ingesting and retaining.

definition: Identifies the source, assessor, sample period, sample size, rubric version and assessment date.
mandatoryAttributes: Log source; assessment date; assessor; sample size; sample period; method; rubric version
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Records prerequisite data-quality gates that must pass before cyber value is scored.
mandatoryAttributes: Minimum parse rate; timestamp and timezone result; schema stability result; overall gate result; failure reason
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Confirms that the sampled events meet the minimum successful parsing threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Measured parse rate; minimum threshold; result; evidence
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Confirms that usable event timestamps and timezone context are present and reliable.
mandatoryAttributes: Timestamp present; timezone present; timestamp quality reference; result
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Confirms that the source schema is sufficiently stable across the assessed sample.
mandatoryAttributes: Schema version; stability result; observed drift; evidence
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Records whether scoring may proceed.
mandatoryAttributes: Pass or fail; decision; date
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Records why a prerequisite gate failed and the remediation required.
mandatoryAttributes: Failed gate; reason; owner; remediation; due date
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Measures the proportion of source information that cannot already be reconstructed from currently ingested telemetry.
mandatoryAttributes: Reconstructible percentage; marginal novelty percentage; subscore; overlapping sources; evidence method
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Measures the proportion of events containing at least one usable investigative join or pivot key.
mandatoryAttributes: Events with pivot key; total events; percentage; qualifying fields; subscore
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Measures whether events explain what happened and the result through fields such as action and outcome.
mandatoryAttributes: Action completeness; outcome completeness; combined percentage; subscore
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Measures how many distinct investigative join-key types are consistently represented.
mandatoryAttributes: Qualifying pivot types; threshold; field list; subscore
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Measures the proportion of the relevant entity population represented in the sample.
mandatoryAttributes: Entity type; observed entities; total population; coverage percentage; subscore
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Records the weighted absolute cyber-value score and rubric used.
mandatoryAttributes: Raw score; maximum score; percentage; weights; rubric version
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.

definition: Records cyber value relative to estimated daily ingestion volume.
mandatoryAttributes: Value score; estimated GB/day; value per GB/day; measurement period
relationshipRule: Belongs to the governing Log Source Cyber Value Assessment.
