Measures the breadth of distinct investigative context types present in each event and across a representative event file. ICD may be expressed as a count or as a percentage of an approved investigative context catalogue.
entityType: Log Quality and Cyber Value Assessment
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment identity; assessed dataset; catalogue size; event count; distinct context types per event; average context types; average ICD percentage; minimum useful threshold; signal count and percentage; noise count and percentage; evidence; assessor; assessment date; rubric version
relationshipRule: A log source, sourcetype, event type or representative file may have multiple ICD assessments over time. One approved current assessment may support logging-quality, filtering and cyber-value decisions.
notes: ICD counts distinct investigative context types, not raw field count. Duplicate fields representing the same context type must not inflate the result. Use ICD with Event Context Completeness, Required Field Coverage and Data Quality.

definition: Defines the approved set of distinct investigative context types used as the denominator for ICD percentage calculations.
mandatoryAttributes: Catalogue name; catalogue version; context categories; distinct context types; owner; approval date
relationshipRule: Each ICD assessment references one approved catalogue version.
notes: Typical categories include identity, network, host/device, process, object/resource, cloud/tenant, session, time/core and detection/security.

definition: Records the proportion of catalogue context types present in an individual event.
mandatoryAttributes: Distinct context types present; catalogue size; ICD percentage
relationshipRule: One event ICD result belongs to each valid sampled event.
notes: Event ICD (%) = distinct investigative context types present ÷ total catalogue types × 100.

definition: Records the mean ICD across all valid events in the assessed file or sample.
mandatoryAttributes: Valid event count; sum of event ICD percentages; average ICD percentage; average context-type count
relationshipRule: One file-average result belongs to each ICD assessment.
notes: Equivalent calculation: total distinct types observed across valid events ÷ (valid events × catalogue size) × 100.

definition: Defines the minimum number of distinct investigative context types required for an event to be classified as useful signal.
mandatoryAttributes: Minimum type count; equivalent ICD percentage; rationale; owner; rubric version
relationshipRule: Each ICD assessment applies one approved minimum threshold.
notes: The threshold should be calibrated by event family and use case rather than treated as a universal external standard.

definition: Records the percentage of valid events meeting or exceeding the minimum useful context threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Signal event count; valid event count; signal percentage
relationshipRule: One signal result belongs to each ICD assessment.
notes: Signal (%) = events meeting minimum ÷ valid events × 100.

definition: Records the percentage of valid events below the minimum useful context threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Noise event count; valid event count; noise percentage
relationshipRule: One noise result belongs to each ICD assessment.
notes: Noise (%) = events below minimum ÷ valid events × 100. Signal and noise percentages sum to 100% for valid events.

definition: Measures how many of the seven investigative context dimensions—When, Who, Where, What, Outcome, Impact and Correlation—are represented in each event and across a representative event file.
entityType: Log Quality and Cyber Value Assessment
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment identity; assessed dataset; valid event count; covered dimensions per event; event CDC percentage; average covered dimensions; file-average CDC percentage; minimum dimension threshold; useful count and percentage; noise count and percentage; per-dimension coverage; evidence; assessor; assessment date; rubric version
relationshipRule: A log source, sourcetype, event type or representative file may have multiple CDC assessments over time. One approved current assessment may support data-quality, filtering and cyber-value decisions.
notes: CDC measures dimension presence, not the quality or richness of fields within a dimension. Use it with Event Context Completeness and Investigative Context Density.

definition: Records the number of the seven investigative context dimensions represented in an individual event.
mandatoryAttributes: When present; Who present; Where present; What present; Outcome present; Impact present; Correlation present; covered dimension count
relationshipRule: One event dimension-count result belongs to each valid sampled event.
notes: Each dimension contributes at most one count, regardless of how many fields support that dimension.

definition: Records the percentage of the seven investigative dimensions represented in an individual event.
mandatoryAttributes: Covered dimension count; total dimensions; CDC percentage
relationshipRule: One event CDC result belongs to each valid sampled event.
notes: Event CDC (%) = covered dimensions ÷ 7 × 100.

definition: Records the average context-dimension coverage across all valid events in the assessed file or sample.
mandatoryAttributes: Valid event count; total covered dimensions; average dimension count; average CDC percentage
relationshipRule: One file-average result belongs to each CDC assessment.
notes: File-average CDC = total covered dimensions ÷ (valid events × 7) × 100.

definition: Defines the minimum number of covered context dimensions required for an event to be classified as useful.
mandatoryAttributes: Minimum dimension count; equivalent CDC percentage; rationale; owner; rubric version
relationshipRule: Each CDC assessment applies one approved minimum threshold.
notes: A default of 5 of 7 may be used locally but should be calibrated by event family and use case.

definition: Records the percentage of valid events meeting or exceeding the minimum dimension threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Useful event count; valid event count; useful percentage
relationshipRule: One useful-event result belongs to each CDC assessment.
notes: Useful (%) = events meeting minimum ÷ valid events × 100.

definition: Records the percentage of valid events below the minimum dimension threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Noise event count; valid event count; noise percentage
relationshipRule: One noise result belongs to each CDC assessment.
notes: Noise (%) = events below minimum ÷ valid events × 100. Useful and noise percentages sum to 100% for valid events.

definition: Records how consistently each of the seven context dimensions is represented across the assessed file.
mandatoryAttributes: When coverage; Who coverage; Where coverage; What coverage; Outcome coverage; Impact coverage; Correlation coverage
relationshipRule: One per-dimension coverage result belongs to each CDC assessment.
notes: Dimension coverage (%) = events containing the dimension ÷ valid events × 100.

definition: Measures the percentage of valid events that fail an approved minimum investigative-value threshold and are therefore classified as investigative noise.
entityType: Log Quality and Cyber Value Assessment
mandatoryAttributes: Assessment identity; assessed dataset; metric name; minimum useful threshold; valid classified event count; signal event count; noise event count; signal percentage; noise percentage; excluded line count; evidence; assessor; assessment date; rubric version
relationshipRule: A log source, sourcetype, event type or representative file may have multiple INP assessments over time. One approved current result may support filtering, tuning, storage and cyber-value decisions.
notes: INP is threshold-dependent and must record the underlying metric and approved minimum. INP (%) = noise events ÷ valid classified events × 100.

definition: Defines the minimum metric value or classification rule required for an event to be treated as useful investigative signal.
mandatoryAttributes: Metric name; threshold value or rule; rationale; owner; approval; rubric version
relationshipRule: Each INP assessment applies one approved usefulness threshold.
notes: Thresholds should be calibrated by event family and use case rather than treated as a universal external standard.

definition: Records the number of valid events that fail the approved minimum investigative-value threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Noise event count; valid classified event count
relationshipRule: One noise count belongs to each INP assessment.
notes: Excluded or unclassifiable lines are not included in the valid-event denominator.

definition: Records the percentage of valid classified events that fail the minimum usefulness threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Noise event count; valid classified event count; noise percentage
relationshipRule: One INP result belongs to each INP assessment.
notes: INP (%) = noise events ÷ valid classified events × 100.

definition: Records the percentage of valid classified events meeting or exceeding the minimum usefulness threshold.
mandatoryAttributes: Signal event count; valid classified event count; signal percentage
relationshipRule: One signal result belongs to each INP assessment.
notes: Signal (%) = useful events ÷ valid classified events × 100. Signal and noise percentages sum to 100%.

definition: Records blank, malformed or unclassifiable lines excluded from the INP denominator.
mandatoryAttributes: Excluded line count; exclusion reasons
relationshipRule: One excluded-line result belongs to each INP assessment.
notes: Report exclusions separately to prevent invalid data from silently lowering or inflating INP.

definition: Phase 1 assessment that determines whether a platform or data source is valuable, technically feasible, supportable and viable to onboard before detailed design and build.
mandatoryAttributes: Platform ID; Data Source ID; Onboarding ID; phase; decision; value score; readiness score; assurance score; effort rating; supportability modifier; next action
relationshipRule: Platform or Data Source 1:M Viability Assessments; Viability Assessment M:1 Onboarding Record
notes: Pre-onboarding gate; operational assurance starts after onboarding acceptance.

definition: Overall Phase 1 result used to decide whether onboarding proceeds, proceeds with conditions, requires further investigation, is not currently viable or is not justified.
mandatoryAttributes: Viable; Viable with Conditions; Further Investigation Required; Not Currently Viable; Not Justified
relationshipRule: One current decision per assessment
notes: Decision is modified by mandatory gate failures, custom solution supportability, reverse engineering and discovery gaps.

definition: Business, compliance, detection and incident-response value of the proposed source.
mandatoryAttributes: Security use cases; compliance requirement; incident-response value; platform criticality
relationshipRule: One score per viability assessment
notes: Keeps value separate from difficulty so high-value but difficult sources are visible.

definition: Readiness of documentation, schema, integration path, authentication, network, data format, samples, volume and collection prerequisites.
mandatoryAttributes: Documentation; log schema; integration path; authentication; network; sample events; volume estimate
relationshipRule: One score per viability assessment
notes: Major discovery gaps should hold progression into detailed design.

definition: Initial support, ownership, monitoring and operational acceptance readiness before build starts.
mandatoryAttributes: Owner; support team; runbook expectation; monitoring approach; escalation path
relationshipRule: One score per viability assessment
notes: Custom collection or parsing should reduce supportability unless ownership and maintenance model are confirmed.

definition: Combined difficulty, complexity and time-to-implement rating used to size the onboarding effort.
mandatoryAttributes: Difficulty rating; complexity rating; time rating; effort index; duration band
relationshipRule: One effort rating per viability assessment
notes: Effort is intentionally separate from viability and value.

definition: Identifies whether the source requires a custom script, custom technology add-on, custom parser, custom routing or unsupported integration path.
mandatoryAttributes: Custom required; custom type; owner; supportability rating
relationshipRule: Zero or one custom-solution modifier per assessment
notes: Custom solution dependency reduces supportability unless ownership, monitoring and lifecycle management are confirmed.

definition: Identifies where weak documentation and a custom or unsupported integration require manual discovery of API behaviour, schema, fields, timestamps or collection mechanics.
mandatoryAttributes: Documentation availability; reverse-engineering required; discovery scope; evidence required
relationshipRule: Triggered when documentation is limited and custom or unsupported integration is required
notes: Should normally result in Further Investigation Required before detailed design.

definition: Tracks whether schema, field list, sample events, volume, authentication and collection mechanisms still need to be defined.
mandatoryAttributes: Schema discovery; field discovery; collection mechanism discovery; sample events; volume estimate
relationshipRule: Unresolved mandatory discovery items block progression into detailed design
notes: Discovery tasks become prerequisites or remediation actions on the onboarding record.

definition: Formal decision gate that moves a proposed source to detailed technical design, holds it for investigation, defers it or rejects it.
mandatoryAttributes: Decision; gate failures; conditions; required next action; assessor; assessment date
relationshipRule: Controls transition from Phase 1 to Phase 2
notes: Gate should link to evidence and an onboarding record.

definition: Current populated records from Viability Assessments.
relationshipRule: Viability Assessments records classified by TAX-06.01.02

definition: Viable with Conditions • Splunk Cloud • Low Risk
relationshipRule: Current viability assessment classified under TAX-06.01.02
notes: Phase 1 initial consultation and viability gate record.

fields.Custom Solution Type: Supported vendor or Splunk add-on / API input
fields.Required Next Action: Confirm API permissions, required event types, tenant details and sample event coverage before detailed design.
fields.Evidence: Public vendor API documentation; sample authentication event; preliminary volume estimate; identity owner confirmation.

definition: Further Investigation Required • Heavy Forwarder Pool • High Risk
relationshipRule: Current viability assessment classified under TAX-06.01.02
notes: Phase 1 initial consultation and viability gate record.

fields.Custom Solution Type: On-premises custom polling script and custom parser
fields.Required Next Action: Run schema, field and pagination discovery; define ownership for the custom script, credentials, retries, checkpointing and monitoring.
fields.Evidence: Existing script stanza warning; limited API notes; no stable schema document supplied.

definition: Viable with Conditions • Splunk Cloud • Medium Risk
relationshipRule: Current viability assessment classified under TAX-06.01.02
notes: Phase 1 initial consultation and viability gate record.

fields.Custom Solution Type: Vendor-supported API input or approved Splunk add-on
fields.Required Next Action: Validate event coverage, API limits, token rotation and sourcetype/CIM mapping before build approval.
fields.Evidence: Cloud services coverage gap; onboarding record; vendor API documentation; initial sample event request.

definition: Not Currently Viable • Backup Platform • Unknown
relationshipRule: Current viability assessment classified under TAX-06.01.02
notes: Phase 1 initial consultation and viability gate record.

fields.Required Next Action: Identify product owner, export capability, sample events, schema, authentication method and expected volume before a pattern can be selected.
fields.Evidence: Reference catalogue gap only; no mapped component, onboarding record or vendor evidence yet.

definition: Viable – Proceed • Splunk Cloud • Low Risk
relationshipRule: Current viability assessment classified under TAX-06.01.02
notes: Phase 1 initial consultation and viability gate record.

fields.Custom Solution Type: Native Splunk internal logs and supported monitoring searches
fields.Required Next Action: Create the onboarding record, define health checks and map required internal sourcetypes to SIEM platform use cases.
fields.Evidence: Registered Splunk platforms; existing internal telemetry; platform ownership confirmed.
